Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola says filming with drones around training grounds should be illegal after Mauricio Pochettino's first session as Manchester United boss was captured and uploaded online.
Pochettino and his players wer
items.text:
Filming training by drones should be illegal - Iraola
- Published
Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola says filming with drones around training grounds should be illegal after Mauricio Pochettino's first session as Manchester United boss was captured and uploaded online.
Pochettino and his players were clearly visible in the footage, which was shot above United's Carrington training base from a variety of angles and distances.
The drone operater apologised and later took down the footage, with sources telling BBC Sport they are adamant there was no security breach and that they do not intend to take legal action.
Iraola said he was sent the 12 minutes of footage on Thursday - three days before United travel to Anfield for a Premier League match.
"The important part of this is that it shouldn't be legal," he said on Friday. "It happened to United but it could happen to me.
"Yesterday, when Sky Sports had access to our training and the cameras recorded 15-20 minutes, you know who trained and who didn't.
"It's not the matter of the advantage. It's the fact that someone can do this. There's a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things that you have to respect. I don't think it's nice for any club."
Ten outfield players were seen working directly with former United States boss Pochettino in the footage, though it seems unlikely they will all start Sunday's match.
"We've faced each other and obviously he [Pochettino] has a lot of Premier League games behind him that we can look at," said Iraola.
"We can look at games from the US but it's true that they have this small advantage that we don't have references to prepare, because they can go different ways that we honestly don't know right now."
Iraola said he expected United to be "well prepared" as Pochettino's assistants travelled to England to work with the players before the Argentine arrived on Wednesday.
"They have this advantage that we don't exactly know - or at least we don't have the references like we do against other opposition," he said.
"Especially the beginning of the game will be important. We have to adapt to certain things. But we know the players very well."
Liverpool are fourth in the table - 14 places ahead of United.
But they have failed to beat the Red Devils at Anfield in each of the past three seasons, and have lost to Arsenal and Manchester City at home already in this campaign.
"You don't find bigger games than this," said Iraola. "I feel lucky to be here and privileged to be a part of these games.
"We have to acknowledge the importance of the game. There are a lot of ingredients. They have a new manager, new challenges for us. This is important for us in a lot of different ways.
"We want to improve our form at home. We have been very good away but not good at home and the first chance we have is United on Sunday."

items.title: Why there are still no non-WebKit browsers on iOS
items.summary:
Why there are still no non-WebKit browsers on iOS

items.text:
Why there are still no non-WebKit browsers on iOS
Firefox on iPhone is growing fast across the world. This is especially true in the EU since 2024, when the EU Digital Markets Act (DMA) started requiring Apple to let people choose their default browser; millions have picked Firefox, and daily use on iOS has doubled. People want to choose the browser on their phone.
But there remains an important limitation to what is available on iPhones: Apple forces all browsers on iOS to be built on Apple’s own browser engine.
This has meant that companies like Mozilla cannot easily bring the full range of Firefox features and functionality to iPhone users because many of these are built within our browser engine, Gecko. iPhones and iPads are unique in having this restriction. On all other major operating systems, including Apple’s macOS, people can access the Gecko-powered version of Firefox.
As a result of the DMA, Apple began allowing alternative browser engines on iOS in the EU. It published a set of conditions that companies like Mozilla must comply with to bring their own browser engine. At the time we said Apple’s rules made it “as painful as possible” for alternatives like Gecko. In the meantime, Japan also introduced new rules requiring alternative browser engines on iOS. Apple applied very similar conditions in Japan to those in the EU.
Nearly three years since Apple introduced these conditions in the EU and almost a year since Japan, not one developer has been able to launch a non-WebKit browser on iOS. The reason is simple: Apple’s conditions remain unworkable. The real test of any rule is whether it delivers the change it was meant to achieve in practice. Compliance on paper alone falls short of that test.
Since the DMA came into effect we’ve been working behind the scenes to test and improve Apple’s conditions so that we can bring Gecko to iOS users. Those efforts have so far largely failed.
One of the conditions requires us not to disclose non-public information related to the project, but here’s an example of what we are up against: to use Gecko, we can’t simply update the Firefox app people already use and love. We’d have to build a whole separate app, a second Firefox. Then we’d have to ask every Firefox user to download it, move their bookmarks, passwords and history across, and manually switch over, step by confusing step.
That’s a lot to ask of people who already made their choice. A significant proportion of people would understandably give up, including many who picked Firefox from the EU’s choice screen.
The conditions Apple imposes, including a level of user friction Apple would never accept for its own apps, mean that the open door feels more like a trap door.
Firefox users on iPhone chose an independent browser. They should get everything that comes with it, including Gecko, the last major browser engine not developed by a big tech company. We’ll keep pushing for a real level playing field, not an opening that drops independent browsers through the floor.

items.text:
In the midst of dealing with the fallout from its ouster of CEO Jensen Huang, Nvidia delivered its latest earnings report this week, with healthy growth and promises that the good times will continue.
On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Anthony Ha, and Tim De Chant discussed what the future holds for Nvidia and the broader AI industry, especially as Anthropic goes public and puts the industry’s circular funding model to the test.
Theresa Loconsolo is an audio producer at TechCrunch focusing on Equity, the network’s flagship podcast. Before joining TechCrunch in 2022, she was one of 2 producers at a four-station conglomerate where she wrote, recorded, voiced and edited content, and engineered live performances and interviews from guests like lovelytheband. Theresa is based in New Jersey and holds a bachelors degree in Communication from Monmouth University.
You can contact or verify outreach from Theresa by emailing [email protected].
Anthony Ha is TechCrunch’s weekend editor. Previously, he worked as a tech reporter at Adweek, a senior editor at VentureBeat, a local government reporter at the Hollister Free Lance, and vice president of content at a VC firm. He lives in New York City.
You can contact or verify outreach from Anthony by emailing [email protected].
Kirsten Korosec is a reporter and editor who has covered the future of transportation from EVs and autonomous vehicles to urban air mobility and in-car tech for more than a decade. She is currently the transportation editor at TechCrunch and co-host of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast. She is also co-founder and co-host of the podcast, “The Autonocast.” She previously wrote for Fortune, The Verge, Bloomberg, MIT Technology Review and CBS Interactive.
You can contact or verify outreach from Kirsten by emailing [email protected] or via encrypted message at kkorosec.07 on Signal.
Tim De Chant is a senior climate reporter at TechCrunch. He has written for a wide range of publications, including Wired magazine, the Chicago Tribune, Ars Technica, The Wire China, and NOVA Next, where he was founding editor.
De Chant is also a lecturer in MIT’s Graduate Program in Science Writing, and he was awarded a Knight Science Journalism Fellowship at MIT in 2018, during which time he studied climate technologies and explored new business models for journalism. He received his PhD in environmental science, policy, and management from the University of California, Berkeley, and his BA degree in environmental studies, English, and biology from St. Olaf College.

items.title: Tom Brady in talks over buying Chelsea stake after Birmingham City exit
items.summary:
Tom Brady is in discussions about buying a small stake in Chelsea. The NFL legend sold a minority share in Birmingham City after three years this month, a move sources have told the Guardian was to pave the way for investing at Stamford Bridge.
Brady was a guest of Chelsea when Enzo Maresca’s then s
items.text:
Tom Brady is in discussions about buying a small stake in Chelsea. The NFL legend sold a minority share in Birmingham City after three years this month, a move sources have told the Guardian was to pave the way for investing at Stamford Bridge.
Brady was a guest of Chelsea when Enzo Maresca’s then side won the Club World Cup in New Jersey last year and was seen celebrating with the players after their remarkable 3-0 final win over Paris Saint-Germain.
The seven-time Super Bowl winner is understood to have a good relationship with Behdad Eghbali, whose fund Clearlake Capital owns 86.5% of Chelsea after Todd Boehly and Mark Walter sold their shares in September.
Brady bought into Birmingham in August 2023, less than a year after his second and final retirement from the NFL, after the club’s takeover by Tom Wagner’s Knighthead Capital.
Brady was appointed chair of the club’s advisory board and had a prominent role in the 2025 Amazon Prime documentary Built in Birmingham: Brady & The Blues, which made headlines when he questioned the “work ethic” of the then manager Wayne Rooney.
In announcing Brady’s departure the club said: “Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years.”
Brady owns a minority stake in the NFL team Las Vegas Raiders, which he purchased alongside Wagner.
Chelsea declined to comment.

items.text:
Celtic's Baur out for 10 weeks, says O'Neill
- Published
Mika Baur will be out for around 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage, Celtic manager Martin O'Neill has revealed.
The 22-year-old twice-capped Germany midfielder went off in the recent 1-0 win at home to Kilmarnock and withdrew from his nation's under-21 squad for this month's international break.
Baur, who moved to Glasgow from Paderborn in August, has made 19 appearances so far this season, scoring four times,
"He'll be out for some considerable time," O'Neill explained.
"It's a real shame - he was playing great for us. There's talk about 10 weeks. There's things that he can't do for a while. Foot's in the boot.
"He was on fire. It is a blow. It seemed so innocuous at the time.
"I thought that he'd been kicked, but it was the other foot he landed on. He's just gone over on it."
Benjamin Nygren missed the second of Sweden's recent double-header and O'Neill cast doubt on the midfielder's participation in Saturday's home Scottish Premiership meeting with St Mirren (15:00 GMT).
"Nygren didn't train today, but we'll see how he is in the morning - he's got a sore heel," the manager said on Friday. "He's been feeling it for a couple of weeks."
O'Neill 'absolutely looking at players' for January
O'Neill's reigning champions are four points clear at the top of the league, having played a game more than nearest challengers Rangers.
The manager says his side have "got to play better" and "be more aggressive going forward".
On the prospect of January additions, O'Neill added: "We're definitely looking at players, wanting to strengthen the squad, which I think we would have to do.
"When people are fit, we will have numbers. We need a bit of quality.
"It would be lovely if, by January, we still had a chance of qualifying for the knockouts of the Europa League. The next couple of games will probably make that decision for us. Hopefully, it's not the breaking point of getting players in.
"I think that we would be doing something. We're absolutely looking at players now.
"I suppose every single club is doing that. The quicker you could get somebody in the better."

items.text:
Omar Berrada interview: Manchester United chief executive on Michael Carrick, Mauricio Pochettino, recent transfer activity and the club hierarchy
Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has spoken exclusively to Sky Sports about the start to the season; the United CEO discusses replacing Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino, the futures of Bruno Fernandes and JJ Gabriel, transfer activity and the Man City charges
Friday 20 November 2026 14:43, UK
In a turbulent time at Manchester United, chief executive Omar Berrada has sat down exclusively with Sky Sports about United's start to the season, the decision to change head coach and facing fan criticism about the club's leadership.
With United in the relegation zone, the club sacked Michael Carrick during the November international break and replaced him with Mauricio Pochettino, who will take charge of his first game away at arch-rivals Liverpool, live on Sky Sports, this Sunday.
The change in head coach has followed a tumultuous opening few months of the campaign, with Lisandro Martinez also taking aim at the club's technical director Jason Wilcox for not preparing the team well enough in the transfer window, while Fernandes also criticised Carrick and his coaching staff's methods.
In this exclusive sit-down interview with Sky Sports' Patrick Davison, Berrada discusses:
- How the club accepts that a lot of the criticism at the club's leadership is fair, but some of it crosses the line
- Not only why Carrick was sacked, but why United stuck with him in the summer
- Why Pochettino is the right man going forwards and the "buzz" he has brought so far
- How the club are defiant they have improved the United squad, despite criticism over their transfer activity
- How captain Bruno Fernandes' contract talks are going and why JJ Gabriel left the club
- His involvement in the Manchester City charges
Berrada believes United are going in the right direction, even though the club currently sit in the Premier League relegation zone ."One hundred per cent," he says.
"I know it's difficult to say this when you're sitting 18th in the Premier League table. It's clear - it's not good enough, not acceptable, and that's why we've made the change that we've made, so that we can move forward.

"But we are laying the foundations for sustained growth to put us in a position where we can be competitive consistently.
"The foundations are there. I am convinced that we are heading in the right direction."
Read below to see the best of the United chief executive's interview…
'We accept the criticism - but some of it does cross the line'
This is the third season in a row in which United have changed their head coach in the middle of the season.
This season strongly resembles the 2024-25 campaign that saw United decide to stick with Erik ten Hag despite the club speaking to other potential candidates - only to replace him with Ruben Amorim a few months into the new season.
As a result, the United leadership team has been questioned - even more so after United defender Martinez publicly criticised technical director Wilcox over the transfer window just gone.
Asked if it has been difficult to see the fan criticism about the hierarchy, Berrada says: "It is. I'm not going to lie. But let's be clear, we're not the protagonists. This is not about the individuals, this is about the club.
"This is about doing everything we can to make our fans happy, and that means improving the results on the pitch, and that means getting a team that is performing to its maximum potential, that the fans can feel proud of.
"Being in this position comes naturally with the criticism and the scrutiny that we're going to get. We accept it, some of it is fair, some of it does cross the line.
"I think we do live in this world of social media, where people like to generate negative stories about the club because it drives more engagement, and it drives more general noise and activity around the club. But we park that."
There are lessons to be learned as well. "If you think about the fact that we've had three permanent managers in less than three seasons, clearly we haven't achieved the stability that we want to - that's for sure," Berrada adds.
"There are different circumstances as to why it didn't work out with Erik, Ruben and now Michael. And we're always learning. We're always trying to improve and understand what has failed."
However, while Berrada recognises the club's leadership hold responsibility for the club's success on and off the pitch, that responsibility also filters down to the players and coaches.
"It is our responsibility to run the club," he says. "And, yes, coaches have a very important role to play. Players, of course, have to perform at the highest level consistently for any coach.
"They're part of a club that when you're wearing the shirt, you have an enormous amount of responsibility. And that responsibility means that you have to be giving your best every day in training, in the matches. And that's the same for executives.
"So I understand the frustration from the fans. It's absolutely normal. My commitment is that we're going to do everything we can to make sure that we put ourselves in a position where we're competing to win titles consistently."
At the centre of United fan disgruntlement is the continued running of the club by the Glazer family, who work alongside INEOS chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe at the very top of the structure. Berrada insists, however, that the dual-running of the club is working.

Mikel Arteta says his Arsenal players have been warned against inadvertently leaking team news via Fantasy Premier League.
The intervention comes after Christos Tzolis selected and captained himself in his Fantasy Premier League (FPL)
items.text:
Arteta warns Arsenal players over FPL team news leak
- Published
Mikel Arteta says his Arsenal players have been warned against inadvertently leaking team news via Fantasy Premier League.
The intervention comes after Christos Tzolis selected and captained himself in his Fantasy Premier League (FPL) team before Arsenal's match against Liverpool on 1 November, after he had missed a month through injury.
The Gunners manager picked the winger in Arsenal's starting XI at Anfield in what was his first appearance since Greece's Nations League draw with the Netherlands on 1 October.
Before Saturday's match at Newcastle, Arteta said he had to speak to his squad, and those close to the club, about their FPL selections.
"With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well," he said
"They're constantly asking me about this as well, because they want to know. It's a topic.
"This is the kind of thing that is happening in our society right now. It's something new. We haven't dealt with it before and we need to put new things in place.
"Obviously, confidentiality is something critical because it's about trust and about what you are trying to do and that should be kept as a huge secret. We'll take measures to make sure it doesn't happen."
The Spaniard also said his players are restricted from selecting themselves in their FPL line-ups.
In October, a number of FPL teams connected to staff and players at Chelsea removed striker Joao Pedro from their teams, hinting the Brazilian had sustained an injury.

There was a dayslong Outlook outage. A nationwide ground stop for only the second time in 25 years. Banks seemed to suddenly stop working. Even iCloud couldn’t stay up and running. This week, it felt like the technological world simply collapsed. And it felt like this might be the beginning of something even bigger.
The week everything fell apart
On The Vergecast: Is AI breaking the world? And is Jensen Huang coming back to Nvidia?
On this episode of The Vergecast, Nilay and David go through the week’s many calamities, and try to explain both what happened in each case — which was generally much milder than the conspiracy theories would have you believe — and why all these small issues might still add up to something worth worrying about. In a world filled with more AI and fewer humans, we’re going to see new kinds of problems and often struggle to find the fixes.
After that, the hosts discuss the latest in the Jensen Huang / Nvidia scandal, which is increasingly less about affairs and more about the allegedly very big business of illegally smuggling chips to China. Huang will not be back as Nvidia CEO anytime soon, no matter what a bunch of X users want, and the fallout of his exit seems likely to only increase.
Finally, in the lightning round, it’s time for Brendan Carr is a Dummy, Nilay’s experience with his always-listening Apple Watch, Google’s inability to name products, and much more.

items.text:
Tech companies are racing to figure out how AI can make everyday work a little easier.
From notetakers to webcams that follow your movements, here are AI-powered gadgets worth checking out if you want to upgrade your workspace.
Flowtica Scribe Pen ($159)
If you’re constantly scribbling notes during meetings, Flowtica’s Scribe could save you from having to type everything up afterward.
The AI-powered pen combines traditional handwriting with audio recording. You can use its built-in gel pen to take notes, tap the side to highlight important points, and press the end of the pen to start recording audio. Once the meeting is over, its AI can transcribe the conversation, summarize key takeaways, and create a to-do list based on what was discussed.
You can even ask the AI questions about the meeting to find specific information without having to go through the entire recording.
The Scribe comes with a built-in microphone and 32GB of onboard storage. It can also identify up to 15 different speakers and supports 92 languages.
Anker Soundcore Work ($159)
Anker’s AI-powered recording pin, Soundcore Work, is designed to capture conversations, meetings, and quick voice memos without taking up much space on your desk.
Priced at $159, the coin-sized device comes with a puck-shaped charging case and can record for up to eight hours on a single charge, extending to 32 hours when used with its case. Anker also claims a recording range of up to five meters, making it useful for capturing conversations around a meeting table.
The companion app handles transcription and uses AI to turn recordings into more organized notes and summaries. Users also get 300 minutes of free audio transcription each month.
If you need more recording capacity or access to additional AI features, Anker offers optional subscription plans, including Pro ($99 per year) and Unlimited ($239 per year).
Logitech MX Keypad ($99)
Logitech’s MX Keypad brings AI shortcuts directly to your desk, with dedicated buttons that let you launch your preferred AI assistant or trigger specific productivity tools with a single press. If you frequently switch between different apps and AI assistants, having these shortcuts within reach could make your workday easier.
The keypad can be configured to work with tools such as GitHub Copilot and Claude Code, along with a range of popular productivity and creative apps, such as OpenAI Codex, Microsoft Teams, PowerPoint, Excel, Notion, Slack, Photoshop, Final Cut Pro, Zoom, and Figma.
Kindle Scribe Colorsoft ($629)
Amazon’s Kindle Scribe Colorsoft brings color to the company’s digital note-taking lineup, and also offers some neat AI features designed to clean up your messy notes.
Starting at $629, the device is aimed at people who regularly work with digital documents, including students, researchers, and professionals who prefer annotating files rather than printing them out. It lets you highlight important passages, mark up documents, organize handwritten notes, and sketch out ideas.
Notably, the Scribe Colorsoft incorporates AI-powered tools to clean up messy handwriting, straighten highlighting and underlining, summarize notes, and help turn scattered thoughts into more organized information. Its search feature can look across your saved notes to find specific details and help identify connections between different entries.
Insta360 Link 2 Pro ($249)
If you’re tired of adjusting your webcam during video calls, Insta360’s Link 2 Pro aims to take care of that for you.
Priced at $249, this AI-powered webcam combines 4K video capture with intelligent tracking and automatic framing. Its smart video tracker can follow your movements and adjust the camera’s position to keep you in view, even when you move around your workspace, which is particularly useful for people who regularly give presentations, teach online, or switch between sitting at their desk and standing during video calls.
The camera also offers group tracking, which can come in handy during team meetings or presentations involving multiple people. AI-powered noise cancellation is another useful addition, helping reduce distracting background sounds during calls.
Autonomous Desk Pro ($599)
Your desk could probably use a little intelligence, too. Autonomous Desk Pro is an adjustable standing desk designed to encourage healthier habits throughout the workday.
Beyond switching between sitting and standing positions, the AI-powered desk uses built-in sensors to monitor your activity and remind you when it’s time to move, stretch, or change positions. It can track how much time you spend sitting versus standing, giving you a better idea of your daily work habits.
The AI features go a step further by allowing you to ask questions about your activity. For example, you can check how long you’ve been sitting, compare your activity with the previous day, or get information about the room’s CO2 levels to help determine whether it’s time to open a window.

items.text:
Key questions as Scottish Premiership returns
- Published
The Scottish Premiership returns with an all-action Saturday after what was a bleak international break for the national side.
Most of the intrigue is on men who will not make a pass or a tackle. There is one new manager, one who is being touted for the Scotland job, another who has turned around a failing side and one who is increasingly under pressure.
And none of those are in charge of Old Firm teams. The managerial status at Celtic and Rangers is relatively settled, but of course that can change in the space of 90 minutes.
This is your essential guide to Saturday's action.
Will Frick make Aberdeen tick?
Aberdeen have a new head coach for their basement battle with Kilmarnock, with Mario Frick replacing Stephen Robinson
The Liechtensteiner was a fine striker in his day and his main mission is to get the Dons firing in front of goal again.
Frick favoured two up top while in charge of Luzern, so he needs to find a way to supply Kevin Nisbet and Ayoub Mouloua.
Connor Ronan could hold the key to improving a sorry set of attacking statistics, but the Irish midfielder will need to show more than he has since his summer arrival.
Aberdeen have 12 goals from 12 league games. Kilmarnock have 13 from 13. Both sides have amassed just four points from their past six outings, so this may well be something of a scrap.
Killie were slightly more menacing in a 0-0 draw at Pittodrie in September and the same could be said of a League Cup quarter-final at Rugby Park a week later, although the Dons did well to prevail on penalties after a red card early in the second half.
The Ayrshire side have the league's worst defensive record by a distance, conceding three or more goals on six occasions. However, manager Neil McCann will have been heartened by a tenacious showing in the 1-0 loss at Celtic Park last time out.
With four successive matches coming against sides currently in the bottom six before taking on the Dundee duo, McCann will view this pre-Christmas sequence as vital.
What about the top?
Of the leading sides, Celtic have the easier-looking task at home to St Mirren, who have enjoyed just one victory in their past 40 visits to the east end of Glasgow in all competitions.
However, the league leaders have not kicked on since thrashing Heart of Midlothian last month, drawing with Dundee United and losing to Falkirk either side of narrow and unconvincing wins over Hibernian and Kilmarnock.
That 1-0 win at home to Killie was just a second clean sheet in seven Premiership matches for the champions.
Celtic came from behind to win 2-1 in Paisley in September, with Yang Hyun-Jun grabbing the second. The winger's return should add dynamism to their attack.
Since pushing Celtic all the way at home, St Mirren have picked up a mere four points from nine matches.
Rangers go to Motherwell off the back of a 2-0 win away to the Buddies, extending their unbeaten league run to 10 games and maintaining the best defensive numbers in the table.
The goals came from a contentious penalty and a deflected shot and manager Derek McInnes spoke of the need to sharpen up in the final third after several promising situations broke down.
After a six-game losing slump that began in Govan, Motherwell have steadied the ship and played out an entertaining 1-1 draw with Dundee United before the break that included a combined 40 efforts on goal.
Well shared the points with Rangers at Fir Park last season, scoring late on both occasions, and, while not the force they were after so many departures, still retain a core of players who celebrated victory at Ibrox in April.
Rangers have the momentum, although recent draws away to Dundee and Hearts underline the fact they remain a work in progress under McInnes.
- New manager Frick to take Aberdeen back to basics 
  - Published19 hours ago
- We'll only sell if offer makes club blink - McInnes 
  - Published21 hours ago
Can in-form Falkirk keep firing?
Five wins on the spin have propelled Falkirk up to third place and they will be big favourites to extend that run at home to St Johnstone.
Celtic beaten, Hearts hammered... fans are talking about European qualification, having ended a five-year stint in League 1 in May 2024.
John McGlynn continues to work his magic on a meagre budget, with new arrivals Jacob Murrell, Owen Eames, Finley Barbrook and Deniss Melniks hitting the ground running.
Ethan Ross is lapping up a new lease of life, while older heads Scott Bain and Liam Henderson have never been better, although the loss of influential skipper Brad Spencer is a huge blow.
The Perth Saints will be no pushovers. They too are punching above their weight with just four defeats in 13 on their return to the top flight.
Rangers are the only side to beat Simo Valakari's men since a 1-1 draw with Falkirk at McDiarmid Park in mid-September.
That was the first league meeting of the clubs since 2010, but, with such astute managers in place, it looks like this can remain a top-flight rivalry for a good while yet.
Reversal of fortunes for capital clubs?
Have Hibs turned a corner and have Hearts fallen down a hole?
Marink Reedijk lost his first three games after replacing David Gray, but now the Hibs head coach is looking for a third successive victory at home to Dundee United.

Friday 20 November 2026 10:15, UK
On the latest episode of Weekend Winners, the panel reveal their top ante-post bets for the upcoming winter months.
Host Kate Tracey looks to next week's Coral Gold Cup at Newbury for her selection, with panellists Declan Rix and Sam Boswell setting their sights on races on the horizon.
Declan Rix...
"I like an old favourite of the show who has returned in good order this season in King Turgeon for the Becher Chase. He is in both the Grand Sefton and the Becher, but he must run in the Becher. He is such a good jumper, and he has won a Grand Sefton before.
"He is a horse that is so, so progressive and last season was a disaster. He has had a wind operation, and he looked like he took a blow at Aintree. We saw signs of life in the stable of David Pipe; he will be for me at a good price."
Kate Tracey...
"I'm aiming for the Coral Gold Cup next week and I like Miami Magic for that. His chasing debuts weren't anything special when getting beat at short prices but he got his act together later on in the season.
"He ran well over hurdles in a Pertemps qualifier last month which gave him a perfect prep. He is a second-season chaser, which means he fits the perfect profile for the race and he's a good price for this race. Hopefully he can go well."
Sam Boswell…
"With plenty of the possible King George VI field not looking likely to turn up, it's more and more obvious to just back Kitzbuhel for the race on Boxing Day. He's Kempton proven, the ground he is proven on - I think the race will decimate and I think he is the one that we will see this weekend for a prep and then kick on to here."

items.title: Southampton give head coach Eckert new deal
items.summary:
Southampton give head coach Eckert new deal
- Published
Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert has signed a new contract at the Championship club until 2029.
The 33-year-old German's existing deal was expiring at the end of this season after being handed the role permanently last December.
Eckert's fut
items.text:
Southampton give head coach Eckert new deal
- Published
Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert has signed a new contract at the Championship club until 2029.
The 33-year-old German's existing deal was expiring at the end of this season after being handed the role permanently last December.
Eckert's future was thrown into doubt over the summer, having been at the centre of an investigation by the Football Association over his role in the 'Spygate' scandal.
He could have been handed a lengthy suspension that would have threatened his job, but was ultimately given a suspended six-week ban and £28,000 fine.
"I'm very happy we have come to the point that we can make it official now," Eckert told the club website., external
"We've had some conversations that started a couple of weeks ago, and the goal was always clear: to show the same commitment we have had for the last 12 months.
"There is a lot that has happened in the last 12 months but the commitment from the club, from [owner] Dragan (Solak), [technical director] Johannes (Spors) and [chief executive] Phil (Parsons), and the supporters, means everything to me.
"I am very grateful for that. We have started a journey that is not even halfway through - there is a lot more to come."
Last season, Eckert, after taking over from the sacked Will Still, led the Saints from 21st in the table to a fourth-placed finish, also reaching the FA Cup semi-final where they took the lead before being beaten by Manchester City.
They were set to face Hull City in the play-off final but were thrown out after admitting spying on three clubs including Middlesbrough before the semi-final.
Saints were also deducted four points before the start of this campaign - if not for that penalty, they would be fourth in the table and one point off the leaders.
Regardless, they have started the campaign well and sit seventh after 15 matches, five points off the automatic promotion places.
Despite last season's controversy, Eckert has been boisterously backed by the Southampton fans at home matches this season.
He signs his new deal exactly a week from before Southampton face Middlesbrough for the first time since the Spygate saga unravelled.
"I think it's a great commitment from both sides; from the club to Tonda, and from Tonda to the club," sporting director Johannes Spors added.
"I'm very happy we have achieved this agreement before the end of the international window, allowing us to go into the busy schedule that is ahead of us with clarity.
"Tonda is very talented and very precise with a great analytical brain, but also has the personality and authority that you need, even at a young age. It is very clear this is the right place for him, and I'm very happy that he feels that too."
Eckert 'highly regarded internally and externally'
BBC Radio Solent's Southampton commentator Adam Blackmore:
This is good news for all parties, but especially for Saints and their players.
Tonda Eckert has effectively signed a new two-and-a-half-year contract, which while not a long deal, gives the club some protection from any admirers who come calling in the future, and gives the players some stability and reassurance.
At 33, Eckert is a coach who, despite the spying scandal of this year, is highly regarded internally and externally.
He and Johannes Spors seem to be building something at Southampton.
He's accrued 96 points from 48 Championship games, pretty remarkable stuff for a first-time head coach, and now Saints' best chance of keeping him until the end of this new deal is if they get promotion this season.
If Eckert can get them up, I already have confidence he can guide them to first-season safety if the club can keep him.

items.title: Uganda restricts cross-border movement, public gatherings amid Ebola threat
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 20 – Uganda has imposed fresh restrictions on public gatherings and cross-border travel in 34 high-risk districts bordering the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) as authorities intensify efforts to prevent another Ebola outbreak.
The measures include a ban on concerts, festivals
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 20 – Uganda has imposed fresh restrictions on public gatherings and cross-border travel in 34 high-risk districts bordering the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) as authorities intensify efforts to prevent another Ebola outbreak.
The measures include a ban on concerts, festivals and political rallies without clearance from the Ministry of Health, alongside mandatory 21-day quarantine or monitored self-isolation for Ugandans returning from the DRC.
The government has also tightened passenger screening at airports, introduced stricter monitoring of hotels and schools, and restricted the movement of humanitarian workers and bodies across its borders.
The restrictions, which took effect immediately, follow concerns over continued movement between Uganda and the DRC, including through unofficial crossing points that could facilitate the spread of the deadly virus.
In a public health advisory issued on November 19, Uganda’s Ministry of Health Permanent Secretary Diana Atwine said the National Task Force on Epidemic Preparedness and Response had approved the additional interventions following an assessment of the risks posed by the outbreak in the neighbouring DRC.
“With the current heightened surveillance, the ministry has observed continued movement of people across our borders, including through ungazetted crossing points, which has increased the risk of the disease entering Uganda and spreading to our communities and to other countries,” Atwine said.
She emphasised that the new directives were additional safeguards, with previously announced restrictions remaining in force.
Under the new guidelines, authorities in the 34 designated border districts have been instructed to monitor new arrivals and people relocating into their communities. Local leaders, particularly Local Council chairpersons, must be notified immediately of new arrivals and movements into the affected areas.
Organisers of mass gatherings will also be required to obtain written authorisation from the Ministry of Health before holding concerts, festivals, political rallies or similar events in the designated districts.
The government has warned that individuals who illegally cross into the country, as well as those who facilitate unauthorised border movements, will face legal action.
Ugandans arriving from the DRC will undergo mandatory health risk assessments before being placed under 21-day quarantine or monitored self-isolation.
The restrictions also extend to humanitarian operations, with aid workers required to obtain clearance from the Director General of Health Services before undertaking cross-border movements.
The transportation of bodies into or out of Uganda will similarly require prior government authorisation.
At Entebbe International Airport, authorities have introduced enhanced screening and infection prevention measures for both arriving and departing passengers.
Travellers will be required to complete passenger locator forms before boarding to facilitate contact tracing, while airlines and other transport operators risk sanctions if they knowingly transport passengers without proper authorisation or documentation.
Uganda has also tightened controls in the education and hospitality sectors. Day scholars travelling between Uganda and the DRC in the designated border districts will no longer be permitted to cross under the new restrictions.
Boarding students who may have been exposed to the virus must undergo 21 days of quarantine in designated facilities before returning to school.
Hotels and other accommodation facilities have been directed to maintain accurate guest registers, verify visitors using valid identification documents and provide the records to health and security authorities when required.
Schools, hospitals, transport terminals, places of worship and other public facilities have also been instructed to provide handwashing facilities and strictly observe infection prevention and control measures.
To strengthen public awareness, radio stations operating in the affected border districts have been directed to dedicate at least two hours every month to Ebola prevention campaigns.
Kenya’s Ebola threat
Uganda’s heightened surveillance comes as Kenya approaches the end of its Ebola monitoring period following an outbreak linked to a traveller who passed through Uganda after arriving from the DRC.
Kenya confirmed its first case on October 6, involving a man who had travelled from the DRC through Kampala before arriving in Nairobi. The patient died on October 5, becoming the index case in the country’s outbreak.
Health authorities subsequently identified eight secondary infections, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to nine. All infections were linked to a single transmission cluster, with no evidence of wider community transmission.
The outbreak claimed two lives, including the index patient and his 65-year-old mother.
Kenya is now working towards a possible declaration of being Ebola-free around December 23, provided no new infections are detected.
The 42-day countdown began on November 12, following the discharge of the last patient and the completion of the mandatory 21-day monitoring period for the final contacts on November 11.
The 42-day period represents twice the virus’s maximum incubation period of 21 days and is the standard requirement for declaring an Ebola outbreak over.
Uganda’s latest restrictions also reflect its own experience with the disease earlier this year, when it recorded 20 confirmed cases between May and June 2026.
The infections comprised 15 imported cases from the DRC and five secondary infections among contacts, with two deaths reported.
Uganda declared its outbreak over on July 28, with the World Health Organisation following on August 27 after the country went 42 days without recording a new confirmed infection.
However, the continued movement of people across its border with the DRC has kept the threat of fresh infections alive.

items.title: Arsenal’s Lisa Baum: ‘I believe in us. I think it’s all about the small margins’
items.summary:
Lisa Baum is 19, for the next few days at least, but you wouldn’t know it. The Germany forward plays with a maturity that explains why she was handed her Arsenal debut in their opening game of the season, less than two months after joining.
Baum had been told that the 2025 European champions had a v
items.text:
Lisa Baum is 19, for the next few days at least, but you wouldn’t know it. The Germany forward plays with a maturity that explains why she was handed her Arsenal debut in their opening game of the season, less than two months after joining.
Baum had been told that the 2025 European champions had a vision for her but that coming in as a young player she would have to be patient. Ten minutes into her debut against Brighton, in Crawley, the young winger scored what would be the winning goal.
“It was unbelievable,” says Baum, speaking in a small meeting room at Arsenal’s London Colney training ground with a maturity that matches her play. “Everything just went so quick. I just shot, my brain was just switched off, it just came out.”
That win kickstarted Arsenal’s season but it quickly stalled. In the league, the team went five games without a win. After a 2-0 defeat by OL Lyonnes in the Champions League on Thursday night, Arsenal have five wins from their opening 15 games. It is far from the season they, or many others, envisioned.
Sunday’s final home game of the year, against West Ham, offers an opportunity to take some positivity into the international break, after which Arsenal face three away fixtures before the winter pause.
“I believe in us,” says Baum. “I think it’s all about the small margins. Sometimes it’s luck, sometimes it’s in the final decision-making, sometimes it’s in how close we are to a goal that doesn’t go in, but we work really really hard in every training session and on trying to keep ourselves up mentally and physically. We’re trying to push through the barrier that we maybe have right now, but we get a lot of trust from the staff and coaches and everybody really believes in each other and I think it’s not going to take long before we’re through this kind of part of the journey.”
Overall, Arsenal have not been playing particularly badly. They have been creating chances and dominating games but struggling to translate that into goals and points. In October, Baum earned a first senior Germany call-up and made her debut off the bench at half-time against Australia, having previously featured for teams from the under-16s to under-23s.
Baum moved to Germany when she was four. Born to a Tanzanian mother and German father, she spent her first years in Dar es Salaam in Tanzania. They swapped a city with a population of about four million for Ahrensbök, a municipality with a population of just over 8,000 near the Baltic coast. “I think my mum had the hardest time, out of us in the family, with the move to Germany,” she says. Baum says she and her brother, Dennis, “learned to adapt easily”.
Baum doesn’t remember her years on the east coast of Africa but when she went back three or four years ago, some sort of memory was triggered. “It was a feeling, or feelings,” she says. “It was so good to grow up there. It was warm, it was the beautiful beaches, it was having all your family around. I was in kindergarten or I was in the water a lot – I love to swim.”
She started playing football after the move to northern Germany, desperate to copy Dennis. “My father played football when he was younger – he was a goalkeeper – but he stopped when he didn’t really enjoy it any more. My mom wasn’t a big fan of me playing; she dressed me like a girly girl, with princess dresses and that kind of stuff, but I was never really like that at that age. I always wanted to follow my older brother – I wanted to wear his clothes. He started playing football before me and I wanted to be like him.”
Baum would play on the side of the pitch at her brother’s club until a parent said she should be playing too. After playing with various local teams she joined Hamburg’s academy. She worked her way into the first team and they won promotion to the second tier in her first season. In the 2024-25 season they reached the DFB-Pokal semi-finals and the top flight. Baum moved to RB Leipzig and scored five goals in 27 games before Arsenal swooped.
“Everything was just so quick,” she says of the move to London. Training required getting used to: “Everything was so sharp, everything was technically excellent, like 10 out of 10. I was quite nervous and had some clumsy actions.”
The transfer also involved swapping an average attendance last season of 1,651 for one of 33,808. “It’s unbelievable,” says Baum, of playing at the Emirates Stadium. “I had only played in a big stadium once before. You can’t even really believe how much the fans give you when you step on the pitch. There’s so much support, that of course we need in this current time. I think Arsenal is a club that holds on to us, on to the team, and gives us a lot of strength.”
Look closely at Baum’s left wrist when she plays and you will usually see a strip of white tape around it. Sometimes it has something written on it. She’s done it “since that day” – the day in 2022 when Dennis died in a car accident, aged 17.
The brother that inspired her on to a pitch is with her on it at the highest level. “The next time I was on the football pitch, I just felt I wanted to do that,” she says. “I feel like it’s given me a different kind of strength and confidence. Sometimes I don’t write anything, but it’s about just having the physical feeling that he is with me.”

The agentic AI capabilities built into operating systems that analyze on-screen information to learn more about the user are “undermining Si
items.text:
Signal is restricting the ability to take screenshots on Android and iOS devices in an effort to prevent AI agents from reading users’ messages and other data. The agentic AI capabilities built into operating systems that analyze on-screen information to learn more about the user are “undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy,” Signal president Meredith Whittaker said in a blog post, while urging OS providers to make it easier for app developers to control what data agents can access.
Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen
Signal will now restrict screenshots on mobile devices, and says AI agents are ‘hostile to privacy.’
“We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy,” Whittaker said. “Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience. This is also the reason we are currently unable to implement these protections on macOS.”
Signal is addressing the privacy concerns by blocking the ability to take screenshots in the app on iOS 27 and Android, which should prevent Siri, Gemini, and other Android AI assistants from reading on-screen content. Users can restore screenshot capabilities in Signal’s app settings, but Whittaker warns that doing so will “potentially expose your (and your contacts’) Signal content to these AI agents, and break our privacy guarantees.” Whittaker admits that Signal’s screenshot blocking remedy is “incomplete,” as it doesn’t address alternative ways that AI agents can access app data, such as retrieving it via the device filesystem.
Signal took a similar approach last year to prevent Microsoft’s controversial Recall feature from capturing secured chats. The encrypted messaging service says it’s struggling to develop a better solution due to the lack of available information regarding how AI agents are actually accessing application data, and is now calling on Apple, Google, and Microsoft to provide “simple technical tools and accurate documentation” to app developers. Signal also says more tools are needed to prevent third-party agents, like Meta’s Muse, from using deep accessibility settings in apps like a “skeleton key” to access application data.
“We all need to recognize that the current integration of AI agents into the operating system, without these common-sense remedies, represents an existential threat to privacy at the application layer, and the ability of independent developers like Signal to protect your sensitive data,” said Whittaker. “Signal is the canary in the coal mine, but this affects the entire ecosystem and should galvanize anyone who cares about these fundamental rights.”

items.title: Liverpool fan found not guilty of racial abuse after Antoine Semenyo withdraws from case
items.summary:
A Liverpool fan accused of racially abusing Antoine Semenyo has been found not guilty after the Manchester City forward withdrew his support for the prosecution.
Semenyo was due to give evidence at Liverpool magistrates court on Friday in the trial of Mark Mogan, 47, who was accused of shouting abus
items.text:
A Liverpool fan accused of racially abusing Antoine Semenyo has been found not guilty after the Manchester City forward withdrew his support for the prosecution.
Semenyo was due to give evidence at Liverpool magistrates court on Friday in the trial of Mark Mogan, 47, who was accused of shouting abuse during the Premier League match between Liverpool and Semenyo’s former club Bournemouth at Anfield on 15 August last year.
But Simon Jones, prosecuting, said: “Following recent contact made with Mr Semenyo, he has indicated he is no longer supportive of proceedings and the prosecution do not consider it is appropriate to compel him. In those circumstances we offer no further evidence in the case.”
District judge Mary Dowrick recorded a verdict of not guilty to the charge of racially aggravated behaviour.
Semenyo, who left Bournemouth for Manchester City in January, had been due to give evidence last month but the trial was adjourned halfway through when Mogan was taken to hospital after a seizure.
The court had heard Mogan, in a wheelchair, shouted racial abuse at Semenyo as he went to take a throw-in about 30 minutes into the game. He was alleged to have said: “Hurry up and take the throw-in, you black bastard.”
Opening the case last month, Mr Jones said: “That racial abuse was shouted directly at Antoine Semenyo, who was close to him. Mr Semenyo briefly froze, as he couldn’t believe what the male had said.”
Mogan then shouted: “I’m talking to you, you cunt,” the court heard. Witnesses also said they saw him throw his chewing gum at the footballer.
Semenyo reported the incident to the referee and Mogan was removed from the stadium at half-time. Mogan, who had an intermediary with him in court, told police in interview that Semenyo had called him a cripple after he shouted at the player to “hurry up”.
Mogan declined to comment as he left court.

items.title: Kindiki pledges to protect judicial independence as budget rises to Sh30.4bn
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 20 – Deputy President Kithure Kindiki has reaffirmed the government’s commitment to protecting the independence of the Judiciary, saying a strong and effective justice system is critical to constitutional democracy, economic growth and social progress.
Kindiki said the administra
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 20 – Deputy President Kithure Kindiki has reaffirmed the government’s commitment to protecting the independence of the Judiciary, saying a strong and effective justice system is critical to constitutional democracy, economic growth and social progress.
Kindiki said the administration recognises the Judiciary’s central role in protecting fundamental rights, resolving disputes, upholding the rule of law and ensuring that government authority is exercised within constitutional limits.
“The Government recognizes that a strong, independent and effective Judiciary is indispensable to constitutional democracy, economic development and social progress,” he said.
Speaking on Friday in Nairobi during the launch of the State of the Judiciary and the Administration of Justice Annual Report for the 2025/2026 Financial Year, the Deputy President said the government’s commitment was reflected in increased budgetary allocations and institutional reforms since President William Ruto assumed office in 2022.
He disclosed that the Judiciary’s budget had increased to Sh30.4 billion in the 2026/2027 financial year, up from Sh27.15 billion in the previous financial year.
Kindiki said the government had also supported the appointment of an additional 53 judges to strengthen the courts’ capacity, address case backlogs and improve the efficiency of justice delivery.
The Deputy President further cited the enactment of the Judges’ Retirement Benefits Act, 2026, which he said addressed longstanding concerns over judges’ retirement welfare and strengthened the independence of the institution.
He noted that President Ruto had also acted on requests by the Judicial Service Commission, including improving judges’ retirement benefits and expediting the issuance of title deeds for court premises.
On Friday, Lands Cabinet Secretary Alice Wahome presented two title deeds covering the Supreme Court precincts and its parking area, ending years of uncertainty over ownership of the land housing the country’s highest court. She also handed over a title deed for a proposed court in Kapsabet town.
“I am glad that we have covered a lot of ground on the promises by the President, including presentation today of title deeds for Supreme Court precincts and the parking area,” Kindiki said.
The Deputy President also pointed to the Judiciary’s improved case clearance rate, noting that for the second consecutive financial year, courts had resolved more cases than were filed.
According to the report, the Judiciary disposed of 576,702 cases against 561,580 new filings during the period, translating to a case clearance rate of 103 per cent.
Of the cases resolved, 190,779 had been pending for more than one year, including 37,757 that had remained unresolved for more than five years.
However, Kindiki challenged the Judiciary to intensify efforts to clear the more than 341,000 cases that have been pending for over a year, warning that delays in the administration of justice undermine public confidence and economic activity.
“The Judiciary must continue playing its rightful role by reducing delays, strengthening commercial dispute resolution and ensuring that justice delivery supports economic and social progress,” he said.
He also announced progress in the implementation of the Judicial Performance Improvement Project Phase II, a Sh26 billion infrastructure programme approved by Cabinet in June in partnership with the World Bank.
The project targets the modernisation of the Supreme Court and Court of Appeal, consolidation of infrastructure for tribunals and Judiciary administration, as well as the establishment of a permanent home for the Kenya Judiciary Academy.
Kindiki said the investments would address infrastructure gaps, improve working conditions and strengthen the Judiciary’s institutional capacity.
He further assured that outstanding legislative proposals, including the Tribunals Bill and the Kenya Judiciary Academy Bill, as well as the review of the Small Claims Court Act, were being fast-tracked.
The Deputy President maintained that investment in the justice system should receive the same attention as infrastructure development, arguing that an efficient Judiciary provides the legal certainty needed to attract investment and support enterprise.
“Just as we invest in roads, energy and digital connectivity to support economic activity, we must invest in a justice system that provides legal certainty, protects rights and facilitates investment and enterprise,” he said.

items.text:
San Francisco 49ers: Kyle Shanahan's side training at altitude in Colorado ahead of Minnesota Vikings clash in Mexico City
San Francisco 49ers are looking to extend their record to 8-1 with a victory against Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City on Monday; the team travelled to Colorado last Sunday and have been training at altitude this week: watch the game live on Sky Sports NFL
Friday 20 November 2026 12:24, UK
San Francisco 49ers are preparing for their upcoming clash against Minnesota Vikings at Mexico City's Estadio Azteca by training 7,258 feet above sea level in Colorado.
The 87,523-capacity stadium is situated at an altitude of 7,349 feet, and Kyle Shanahan's side are hoping to gain every advantage to improve on their 8-1 record this season against the Vikings on Monday morning, live on Sky Sports NFL.
Their training facility in Santa Clara, California, is at sea level, and the 49ers travelled to the Air Force Academy in Colorado on Sunday, following their 46-40 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
- Who is NFL MVP favourite? 'He is head and shoulders above'
- Latest NFL fixtures, results and UK kick-off times
- Get latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract
Kevin O'Connell's Vikings chose to practise in Minnesota rather than try to adjust to the altitude ahead of time.
The 49ers have historically altered their schedule to account for where games are played. They previously trained at the Air Force Academy four years ago in preparation for a game against Arizona Cardinals in Mexico City.
"One thing I know about our organisation that I really respect is everybody, from the top down, they'll do anything to try to help us get acclimated to whatever adversities or things that we have to face throughout the week," said running back Christian McCaffrey, who went to high school in Highlands Ranch, Colorado, 41 miles north of the Air Force Academy.
"So if we're going to play at altitude, coming here and getting acclimated is part of that. So I appreciate it."
Prior to week one, the 49ers spent a week in Melbourne, Australia, before their season curtain-raiser against Los Angeles Rams, who flew in shortly before the game.
San Francisco beat the Rams 27-7, looking sharper after adjusting to the 19-hour time difference.
"I think it's been nice to be here at practice and get some workouts in, and even just doing meetings and just living here for a week," quarterback Brock Purdy said.
"It's been a real thing that we've had to adjust to, and I'm glad that we're here. I think it's the right move for sure."
A half-speed training session was held on Wednesday, with Raheem Morris walking to the lectern on Thursday as if he was labouring to breathe the Colorado air.
"I'm out of breath right now," San Francisco's defensive coordinator said.
"You won't see the effect obviously into the game, but definitely good to get out here and get used to it."
Evans and Greenlaw back in training
Wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis) and linebacker Dre Greenlaw (neck) returned to practice on Thursday after sitting out Wednesday.
It was Evans' first practice since he left an October 19 win over Washington. He has missed the last three games.
"I thought he looked great," Purdy said. "He looked just like good old Mike from what I've been throwing him all year.
"Obviously, for me, I'm extremely encouraged by it. I'm going to go back, watch the film, see how it all looked. But just my initial thoughts were he looked great out there."
Evans was doing work on the side at the start of Thursday's session and then took part in drills with the receiving corps. Cornerbacks Renardo Green (back) and Upton Stout (shoulder), safeties Ji'Ayir Brown (ankle) and Siran Neal (foot) and defensive end Khalid Kareem (ankle) took part in the open portion of practice.
The only player not in uniform was back-up quarterback Mac Jones, who sat out with an illness.

items.title: Historical milestone: Kenya’s crude oil drilling kicks off in Turkana County with onshore rig spudding
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 20 – Kenya’s countdown to producing crude oil from its South Lokichar sub-basin oil fields has begun in earnest, following the official spudding of the Gulf Energy E&P BV SEZ Amosing 1 well pad.
In Oil and Gas operations, spudding is the first step in drilling a well and marks th
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 20 – Kenya’s countdown to producing crude oil from its South Lokichar sub-basin oil fields has begun in earnest, following the official spudding of the Gulf Energy E&P BV SEZ Amosing 1 well pad.
In Oil and Gas operations, spudding is the first step in drilling a well and marks the official start of operations.
Following the recent rigging, levelling and commissioning of GW70, an onshore drilling rig leased from Great Wall Drilling Company (GWDC) at the Amosing 1&2 Oil Fields in Turkana County, the Ministry of Energy and Petroleum Cabinet Secretary Opiyo Wandayi presided over the spudding ceremony, effectively kicking off the first phase of the Gulf Energy E&P BV SEZ US$ 6 billion drilling and crude oil production efforts.
Speaking at the spudding ceremony, CS Wandayi, flanked by Ministry of Roads and Transport Cabinet Secretary Davis Chirchir and Ministry of East African Community (EAC) Beatrice Askul among other government officials, confirmed that Kenya’s oil fields development efforts are running on schedule, with 1st December set as the official first oil production day.
On his part, CS Chirchir confirmed that the government is investing more than KShs 24 billion in the development of quality infrastructure projects such as roads in the oil fields region. The development of such infrastructure, he noted will elevate the regions social economic standing.
Describing Kenya’s first oil production agenda as a historical milestone, CS Wandayi said the government is supporting efforts to accelerate development of the oil fields in Blocks T6 and T7, as per the parliamentary-ratified Field Development Plan (FDP).
CS Wandayi stated that in the first phase, as set out in the FDP, Gulf Energy E&P BV SEZ is expected to focus development on the Ngamia, Amosing, Twiga and Ekales fields, together referred to as NEAT, to produce more than 20,000 barrels per day. The six discoveries have a best-estimate recovery of 326 million stock-tank barrels over a 25-year contract period.
“This spudding event by the Government of Kenya’s contractor, Gulf Energy E&P BV SEZ, marks a historical milestone ahead of first oil production,” CS Opiyo said. He added, “I am impressed by the sense of professionalism and patriotism of Gulf Energy E&P BV SEZ and its contractors who are working flat out to meet targets set out in the Field Development Plan.”
The spudding and scheduled first oil production effectively marks Kenya’s entry into commercial crude oil production and is the culmination of the development programme in Turkana County. Gulf Energy E&P BV SEZ will operate the project oil fields under Production Sharing Contracts (PSCs) with the National Government, under the oversight of the State Department of Petroleum and the Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA).
Gulf Energy E&P BV SEZ Managing Director Paul Limoh, while confirming the firm’s system readiness, said the first phase of 20,000 barrels per day production will be transported by road to Mombasa for stockpiling at the Kenya Petroleum Refineries Limited tank farms from 1st December. Beyond the first phase, the company plans to increase production to 50,000 bpd in the project’s second phase,
“At Gulf Energy, we are maintaining a tight delivery and project management schedule with the support of all our stakeholders, with a pledge to deliver against the FDP to world-class standards,” Limoh said. He added, “Overall, we are targeting six discoveries within Blocks T6 and T7. And the six discoveries have a best-estimate recovery of 326 million stock-tank barrels over a 25-year contract period.”
For this first phase, Gulf Energy E&P BV SEZ has contracted Baker Hughes, a leading global Oilfield Services and Equipment (OFSE) solutions provider, to deliver Integrated Well Services. The firm has also engaged SLB, a leading energy technology and services company, to deliver the Early Production Facility (EPF).
Kenya’s crude oil is low in sulphur, asphaltene, and aromatics but moderately high in wax content, with a high wax appearance temperature (WAT) and pour point above ambient conditions. The associated gas is rich and sweet with some localised high carbon dioxide content. The crude oil is expected to be an intermediate, paraffinic, sweet oil with an API gravity of 30.5⁰ and will be indexed to Dated Brent.
Overall, Kenya stands to gain significant fiscal and economic benefits from the South Lokichar Basin oil fields development, which will position the country as a major East African oil producer. The Government of Kenya projects potential lifetime earnings of more than USD 2.9 billion (KES 371 billion), depending on prevailing global oil prices and production volumes over the life of the project.

items.title: Stoke and Birmingham proving you shouldn't judge a book by its cover
items.summary:
Stoke & Blues proving never judge book by its cover
- Published
Stoke City v Birmingham City: Third v first in the Championship.
That is a "tale of two cities" that did not look too likely to get written when Mark Robins' Potters started this season with three straight defeats and Blues won only two
items.text:
Stoke & Blues proving never judge book by its cover
- Published
Stoke City v Birmingham City: Third v first in the Championship.
That is a "tale of two cities" that did not look too likely to get written when Mark Robins' Potters started this season with three straight defeats and Blues won only two of their first eight league games under Chris Davies.
But, just like you should never judge a book by its cover, the footballing equivalent is to never judge any league table until after 10 games.
The season is now three months old - after Saturday's meeting at the Bet365 Stadium it will be more than a third of the way in.
And a clearer picture is starting to emerge as to whether what was once the "worst of times", especially in Stoke's case, might yet become the "best of times" before this 46-game campaign ends.
With 15 games gone, there are three clubs right at the top all on 29 points in what is already looking a ridiculously tight Championship table.
And two of them meet head on in front of an expected full house in the Potteries, having both been bang in form going into the latest international break.
Stoke are on a run of nine wins and only one defeat in 12 league games since the start of September, while Blues have won six out of seven since football returned after the first autumn international break.
So, how will things start to shape up after the second such break?
- EFL preview: Evans' gripes & unexpected departures 
  - Published3 hours ago
'One of most physical XIs in league' - Davies on Stoke
Stoke had the edge last season, winning 1-0 at home in September before drawing 1-1 in the return at St Andrew's in January, prior to Blues going into their late-season decline - and Davies can see the difference in the Potters.
"I watched the game back from when we played them a year ago and it looks very different," the Blues boss told BBC Radio WM.
"He [Mark Robins] has made a big impact from where they were last season. A real stamp of his identity.
"They've gone to a back five and, since then, they've conceded the fewest goals in the league - nine in 12 games.
"They've looked strong, particularly in the central areas. They've got bigger. They're now one of the most physical starting XIs in the league."
While extolling the Potters' defensive qualities, Davies is also well aware they have an attacking threat and he is an admirer of Stoke's American winger Jack McGlynn, who is their top scorer with five goals.
"I already knew a little bit about the boy McGlynn," said Davies. "He's been exceptional with the goals he's got.
"They're a team much like ourselves. I want us to go there as a measure to see how far we've come, if we can display what we've been showing recently."
'They've got some real talent' - Robins on Blues
Stoke boss Mark Robins' main concern is determining the fitness of his international contingent, having had 10 out of his 20-man matchday squad from their 2-1 win at Portsmouth away for almost a fortnight.
Of the 14 players involved that day, Swedish keeper Viktor Johansson, Bosun Lawal (Ireland), Robert Bozenik (Slovenia), Luke Graham (Scotland) and euphoric Northern Ireland pair Ethan Galbraith and Justin Devenny all played, while McGlynn was part of new Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino's USA send-off.
But now focus turns to Birmingham.
"They've changed a little bit," Robins told BBC Midlands Today. "They've clearly taken a lot from the Championship last season.
"They've got some players in form and some coming back from international duty, although less than we have.
"A lot [of their players] have been together a few seasons now - and they've got some real talent. But it gives us a chance to pit ourselves against the team at the top. The last time we did that was against Charlton."
Having already seen off one table-topping team in the Potteries this season, Robins is not getting carried away though.
"It's nice to be where we are," he added. "We've never been in the conversation before and we want to be in that conversation."
Stoke will hold a minute's applause before the game to mark the recent passings of Potters legend Peter Dobing and former manager Gudjon Thordarson.
'Blues taking risks, Stoke resilient' - old boy Clarkson
One local celebrity fan looking forward to Saturday's game more than most is a man with a foot in both camps - ex-Birmingham and Stoke full-back Ian Clarkson.
Boyhood Blues fan Clarkson made 174 appearances for the club between 1988 and 1993, when he moved on to Stoke, where he made a further 95 appearances.
After seeing out his career with Northampton Town, Kidderminster Harriers and Nuneaton Borough, Clarkson, now 55, then took his talents into the press box, reporting on Blues first for the Express & Star then the Birmingham Post - and he now coaches football in his teaching role at Repton College.
He has seen plenty of both clubs this season - and both have taken him slightly by surprise.
"Blues are a lot more inclined to attack than they were last season, they look more likely to take a few risks," Clarkson told BBC Sport.
"The signing of August Priske in January is obviously starting to reap rewards and it's bringing the best out of Jay Stansfield. Plus you've got good contributions coming from their wingers and two more on the bench to come on.
"Blues are playing some lovely football right now. Chris Davies is obviously a manager who works very hard at it. And they just seem to have got it right. They've clicked."
"Stoke are starting to look more like a Stoke City team, in the nicest possible way.
"Mark Robins is just one of those managers who, wherever he is, just seems to get better. The longer he stays at a club the better he gets. And they really do look far more resilient.
"There's something about the place that just feels different this season. They've got the fans back on side and that's more important than anything. Everyone knows how tough a place Stoke can be when it's bouncing."
