items.title: China’s Shenzhen Summit Offers Hope for a More Peaceful World
items.summary: When Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomed US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin to Shenzhen for a historic trilateral summit, the significance extended beyond the presence of three powerful leaders. It was also an opportunity to reaffirm a message the world urgently needs t
items.text:
When Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomed US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin to Shenzhen for a historic trilateral summit, the significance extended beyond the presence of three powerful leaders. It was also an opportunity to reaffirm a message the world urgently needs to hear: peace is precious, dialogue matters, and major powers have a responsibility to work together.
The historic meeting and the Declaration toward Peace that followed offered a reminder that diplomacy is most valuable when relationships are difficult. China, Russia and the United States have competing interests and different political systems. Yet their shared responsibility to safeguard peace should bring them into communication, not push them further apart.
For ordinary people, international stability is not an abstract concept. It is reflected in the price of fuel, the cost of food, the security of jobs, the confidence of businesses and the prospects young people have for their future. When tensions among major powers disrupt energy markets, trade routes or supply chains, households and communities thousands of kilometres away can feel the consequences.
The Shenzhen meeting therefore matters to people who may never follow diplomatic communiqués. A more stable relationship among major powers can help create conditions in which economies trade, businesses invest and countries focus on development rather than uncertainty.
China’s hosting of the summit placed this human dimension of diplomacy in view. Xi described the meeting as positive, constructive and fruitful, and urged the three countries to follow through on their consensus, strengthen communication and promote peace through cooperation. The emphasis was not simply on the leaders’ encounter, but on what sustained engagement could mean for the wider world.
The declaration reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. It also committed the three countries to dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation. These words carry particular weight because the consequences of a nuclear conflict would be catastrophic for humanity, without regard to borders, wealth or political allegiance.
In an age when technology, military capability and geopolitical competition are advancing rapidly, keeping channels of communication open is essential. Dialogue can help reduce miscalculation, clarify intentions and create space for decisions that protect lives. It is not a guarantee of agreement, but it is a necessary safeguard against escalation.
The summit also addressed practical issues that touch people’s lives, including energy security and the stability of supply. The declaration set out plans to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products and reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows. For developing economies, predictable energy markets matter to transport, manufacturing, agriculture and the everyday cost of living.
China has consistently advocated cooperation rather than decoupling and disruption. Xi’s call to combine the countries’ strengths in resources, manufacturing and consumption to expand the benefits of cooperation reflects an approach that sees economic interdependence as an opportunity. When trade and supply chains function reliably, businesses can plan, workers can earn and consumers can benefit.
The discussion of United Nations reform is equally important. As permanent members of the Security Council, China, Russia and the United States acknowledged the need for the UN to respond more effectively to global challenges and fulfil its central mission of maintaining international peace and security. For Africa and other developing regions, a more responsive multilateral system is essential to ensuring that global decisions reflect a wider range of voices and realities.
China’s advocacy for a more representative international order resonates across Africa, where countries seek greater participation in decisions on finance, trade, security and development. African states should be able to engage international partners on the basis of their own priorities, building relationships that support industrialisation, infrastructure, technology, skills and opportunity.
Kenya, for example, depends on international trade, investment, affordable energy and stable markets. It has a practical interest in a world where major powers manage their differences responsibly and where cooperation remains possible across political divides. Peaceful coexistence is therefore not merely a diplomatic ideal; it is part of the environment that allows countries such as Kenya to pursue development.
The Shenzhen summit also reinforces an important principle: countries do not have to abandon their interests to cooperate. Xi has urged China and the United States to make the list of areas for cooperation longer and the list of problems shorter, while managing differences constructively. This recognises that disagreements may persist, but need not define the entire relationship.
The real test will be what happens after the meeting. Declarations acquire meaning through follow-up, regular communication and practical action. The summit cannot resolve every dispute, nor should its importance be measured only by immediate breakthroughs. Its value may lie in keeping dialogue alive and establishing habits of engagement at a moment when the world needs stability.
China’s message from Shenzhen is ultimately a human one. Behind every discussion of strategic stability are families hoping for security, young people seeking opportunity, farmers and businesses needing dependable markets, and communities that want resources spent on conflict to be directed towards better lives.

Nations League quarter-finals: England to face Norway in the last eight with a potential semi-final tie with Germany waiting
England have been drawn to face Norway in the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals; the quarter-finals will be two-leg ties and will take place in the March international break;
items.text:
Nations League quarter-finals: England to face Norway in the last eight with a potential semi-final tie with Germany waiting
England have been drawn to face Norway in the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals; the quarter-finals will be two-leg ties and will take place in the March international break; Wales will face Slovenia and Republic of Ireland will take on Croatia in the A/B play-offs
Friday 20 November 2026 11:45, UK
England will take on Erling Haaland and Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals.
Thomas Tuchel's side finished top of their group thanks to their dramatic 3-2 win over Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium, while Norway finished second behind Portugal in Group D.
The two sides met in the 2026 World Cup quarter-finals, with a Jude Bellingham goal in extra-time sending the Three Lions through to the last four.
Should England progress, they will meet Belgium or Germany in the semi-finals. The other two quarter-final ties have seen world champions Spain drawn with France and Netherlands take on Portugal.
The quarter-finals will be two-leg ties and will take place in the March international break, with the first legs between March 25-27 and the second legs between March 28-30.
This will then be followed by the Nations League Finals, which will be held between June 9 and June 13, 2027.
The tournament will feature two semi-finals, a third-place play-off and the final. The four semi-finalists will be invited to make bids to host the semi-finals and final.

Wales and Republic of Ireland discover play-off opponents
Wales and the Republic of Ireland have also learned who they will face in the Nations League A/B play-offs.
Wales avoided automatic relegation to League B after securing one of the two better last place finishers in League A, while Republic of Ireland finished runners-up in their League B group behind Austria.
Craig Bellamy's side will take on Slovenia, while Heimir Hallgrimsson's men will face Croatia.
The play-off ties will also take place during the March international break.

items.title: James Bowen latest jockey to reveal death threat incident
items.summary:
James Bowen received death threat from disgruntled punter as jockey speaks out following similar Nico de Boinville incident
Bowen brothers were given security protection last year after a threat was made; fellow jockey Nico de Boinville revealed a similar incident earlier this week after threat made
items.text:
James Bowen received death threat from disgruntled punter as jockey speaks out following similar Nico de Boinville incident
Bowen brothers were given security protection last year after a threat was made; fellow jockey Nico de Boinville revealed a similar incident earlier this week after threat made to Nicky Henderson's yard. Warning: Readers may find some of the language in this story distressing
Friday 20 November 2026 12:24, UK
James Bowen has become the latest jockey to reveal he has been subjected to death threats from disgruntled punters, with the 25-year-old disclosing that he and champion jockey brother Sean required security protection following an incident last year.
Nico de Boinville was in the news earlier this week when a threat against his life had been phoned in to Nicky Henderson's yard following the defeat of an odds-on favourite at Plumpton.
That was far from the first incident of its kind, and Bowen, speaking in his DragonSports blog while he recovers from a broken wrist, said both he and his brother regularly receive abuse on social media - but one incident in particular stood out.
- Nicholls breaks record for Jumps wins with Warwick triumph
- Sober Glory storms to victory over Old Park Star on chase debut
He said: "Last season, at Ffos Las on October 16, 2025, we were both the subject of death threats during a race meeting, to the extent that we had security accompanying us between the paddock and weighing room for the next three or four days.
"It was something we kept largely to ourselves at the time, but recent events involving Nico de Boinville have brought the subject back into sharp focus.
"In our case, somebody made an anonymous telephone call, which I believe went to either the racecourse or the British Horseracing Authority, threatening to kill both me and Sean.
"It happened while we were both racing at Ffos Las. We were informed about it and, understandably, the authorities had to take it seriously.
"After our final race, we spoke to the police and explained everything we knew. There was security around us for the following few days, with people accompanying us to and from the paddock.
"Nothing much came of it afterwards, as far as I know, and we never heard anything further about who had made the call."
He went on: "You can perhaps understand why somebody might get frustrated if a horse they have backed gets beaten, but there is absolutely no justification for taking it to that sort of extreme.
"I hope the person who made the threat had no intention of carrying it out, but you cannot simply dismiss something like that.
"What is perhaps even more worrying is that receiving unpleasant messages has become such a regular occurrence that you almost become accustomed to it.
"I have had plenty of messages telling me they hope I break my legs or my neck. They tend to come through private messages on social media, particularly Instagram and X.
"It is not something that surprises me any more, which is probably quite sad when you think about it.
"You get hardened to a certain extent, and there is a bit of dark humour among jockeys about some of the things people send. Sometimes you have to laugh about it because otherwise you would cry."
If you have been affected by this story, support and guidance are available at sky.com/viewersupport

items.title: Gachagua threatens protests against IEBC over 2027 election
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 20 – Democracy for Citizens party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has warned President William Ruto and the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) against manipulating the 2027 General Election.
Gachagua warned that Kenyans would not accept what he described as a rig
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 20 – Democracy for Citizens party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has warned President William Ruto and the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) against manipulating the 2027 General Election.
Gachagua warned that Kenyans would not accept what he described as a rigged election, insisting that the IEBC must address opposition concerns over voter registration, identification cards and the announcement of presidential results before the country goes to the polls.
Speaking on Friday in Wamunyoro a day after a meeting between opposition leaders and IEBC officials, Gachagua claimed that there were worrying differences in how voters were being registered and identification cards issued in different parts of the country.
He alleged that voter registration was being conducted selectively in parts of the Rift Valley, claiming that some residents were receiving assistance to register while people in other regions faced delays.
“We want to know why you are having selective registration of voters in the Rift Valley. At Ruto’s place, votes are being registered, taken to homesteads. Why are you not doing the same in the rest of the country?” Gachagua posed.
He also questioned what he described as unequal access to national identity cards, alleging that some applicants in areas associated with the President were receiving the documents within days while others waited for up to 10 months.
Gachagua said the opposition had raised the concerns during its engagement with IEBC, arguing that unequal access to identification documents could affect the ability of eligible Kenyans to register as voters.
The DCP leader further questioned the time taken to process identity cards, claiming that applicants in some parts of the country waited between eight and 10 months, while others allegedly received them within three days.
Another issue raised by the opposition was the process of tallying and announcing presidential election results.
Gachagua argued that presidential results should be announced at the constituency level, insisting that the process should not depend on further tallying at the national level in Bomas of Kenya.
He maintained that the IEBC chairman’s role should largely be to add up results already declared at constituency level and announce the overall winner.
“The Constitution of Kenya says there shall be a presidential election in the 290 constituencies. The presidential election will be conducted at the constituency and will end there,” he said.
He questioned why presidential results should be taken to Bomas for further tallying, arguing that constituency returning officers should declare the results from their respective areas.
According to Gachagua, counting of presidential votes begins immediately after polling stations close, making it possible for constituency results to be established within hours.
The DCP leader also invoked the 2024 Gen Z protests, warning that Kenyans could mount fresh demonstrations if the electoral commission failed to address their concerns.
He said the protests witnessed during the Finance Bill demonstrations would be minor compared to what could happen if the 2027 election process was compromised.
“Don’t underestimate the resilience and the determination of the Kenyan people. That commotion you saw there during the Finance Bill is child’s play,” Gachagua warned.
He challenged the IEBC to engage political leaders and address the proposed electoral reforms, saying Kenyans were determined to protect the credibility of the next election.
“If you don’t want to engage the leaders, then Kenyans will engage you directly. And I can tell you, you cannot win any battle against the people of Kenya,” he said.
Gachagua maintained that the opposition wanted changes agreed upon before the election rather than waiting until disputes emerged after voting.

items.title: Lenku faces NCIC remedial action over remarks on Maasai political representation
items.summary: NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 20 – The National Cohesion and Integration Commission (NCIC) has faulted Kajiado Governor Joseph Ole Lenku over remarks in which he described political parties that fail to give the Maasai community senior leadership positions as enemies, warning that the statements risked underm
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 20 – The National Cohesion and Integration Commission (NCIC) has faulted Kajiado Governor Joseph Ole Lenku over remarks in which he described political parties that fail to give the Maasai community senior leadership positions as enemies, warning that the statements risked undermining peaceful coexistence.
In its Determination No. 5 of 2026, the commission found that Lenku’s remarks, made during a political gathering in Kajiado County on August 22, 2026, promoted political exclusion and threatened adverse consequences against individuals who chose alternative political paths.
The commission took issue with the governor’s use of the words “adui wetu” (our enemies) to describe political formations that did not accommodate Maasai interests in party leadership and nominations.
It also raised concerns over his warning that those who chose a different political direction would “utajipata taabani” (find yourself in difficulty), saying the language introduced an element of intimidation into political participation.
According to the commission, the remarks went beyond advocating for the political representation of the Maa community and risked alienating other communities living in Kajiado, which is home to people from diverse ethnic backgrounds.
“The remarks fell below the constitutional standard of responsible leadership and posed a risk to peaceful coexistence in Kajiado County,” the commission said.
The inquiry followed a video recording of the political forum in which Lenku addressed the place of the Maasai community in party leadership and nomination processes, particularly positions considered to belong to the Maa community in Kajiado and Narok counties.
Lenku appeared before the commission on September 17, 2026, accompanied by his lawyers and county officials, where he confirmed the factual accuracy of the remarks attributed to him.
However, through his lawyers, AMA Advocates LLP, the governor argued that his statements were made in his capacity as an elected leader and spokesperson for the Maa community, seeking to address historical injustices, land dispossession, marginalisation and political representation.
His legal team maintained that the remarks were directed at political parties and choices rather than ethnic communities, arguing that expressions such as “adui”, “hatuna uhusiano na wewe” and “taabani” referred to political association and electoral competition and did not amount to threats of violence, incitement or ethnic hatred.
The commission, however, rejected the argument that the political context placed the statements beyond its mandate, maintaining that political discourse must comply with constitutional standards on national cohesion and the rights of other citizens.
It said the governor’s position as an elected leader and influential political figure increased the potential impact of his statements, particularly their ability to mobilise supporters and deepen divisions.
The NCIC further acknowledged that demands for community representation, equitable political participation and redress for historical injustices were legitimate issues that could be raised in public debate.
However, it cautioned that such grievances could not justify language that intimidated people or portrayed those pursuing alternative political choices as enemies.
In its assessment, the commission cited Articles 27, 33(3) and 38 of the Constitution, which provide for equality and freedom from discrimination, responsible exercise of freedom of expression and the right to political participation.
Following its findings, the commission issued Lenku with a Notice of Remedial Conciliation proposing corrective, preventive and restorative measures aimed at addressing the concerns raised by his remarks.
The governor has been given seven days from the date of the determination to communicate in writing whether he accepts the proposed terms or wishes to suggest variations.
The commission clarified that its determination was administrative and conciliatory in nature and did not amount to a criminal conviction or a judicial finding of guilt. The proposed measures also do not carry criminal punishment.
It further emphasised that the findings do not restrict the Maasai community or any other group from advocating for political representation, addressing historical injustices or demanding equitable participation in public institutions.
Instead, the commission urged political leaders to pursue such demands through dialogue, democratic engagement and lawful political processes without threatening or excluding other communities.
The determination comes amid continuing political competition over community representation and party leadership in the Maa-dominated counties of Kajiado and Narok, where political alignments and nomination processes have remained sensitive issues.
The NCIC reiterated that political differences should not be allowed to undermine the rights, dignity and security of residents from different communities.

items.title: World Toilet Day: Sanitation must become an affordable investment for every household
items.summary:
By Rose Muyanga,
Access to a safe toilet is fundamental to public health, dignity and well-being. While Kenya has made progress in expanding access to improved sanitation, disparities in household circumstances, infrastructure and affordability mean that more needs to be done to extend these gains t
items.text:
By Rose Muyanga,
Access to a safe toilet is fundamental to public health, dignity and well-being. While Kenya has made progress in expanding access to improved sanitation, disparities in household circumstances, infrastructure and affordability mean that more needs to be done to extend these gains to every community.
The 2025–2026 Kenya Mini Demographic and Health Survey shows that 76 per cent of households have access to improved sanitation facilities. However, the proportion stands at 63 per cent in rural areas, compared with 93 per cent in urban areas. The survey also indicates that 45 per cent of the population has access to at least basic sanitation services, while 7.4 per cent still practise open defecation.
These findings underscore the importance of sustaining investments in sanitation while addressing the different needs of households. Access to an improved toilet is an important step, but safely managed sanitation also requires hygienic and durable facilities supported by appropriate waste containment and management systems.
The Ministry of Health’s Costed National Sanitation and Hygiene Roadmap 2023–2030 provides an indication of the investment required. It estimates that a basic G1 sanitation unit, designed to provide a clean and flyproof toilet, costs between KES 10,000 and KES 12,000 in hardware, depending on county conditions. A more durable individual G2 toilet with safe waste containment costs between KES 25,000 and KES 30,000.
The financial commitment also extends to maintaining good hygiene practices. The Roadmap estimates that basic household hand hygiene costs KES 7,048 annually, covering household promotion, handwashing facilities and soap. This highlights the need for sustained investment in sanitation infrastructure, reliable water access and everyday hygiene practices.
For households managing competing priorities such as food, rent and school fees, meeting these costs can require careful financial planning. Flexible financing arrangements can help spread the cost of improvements over time, enabling families to invest in better sanitation facilities while managing their other financial obligations.
This presents an opportunity for financial institutions to complement ongoing public efforts by developing accessible financing solutions that respond to household needs. These may include financing for durable, all-weather toilets, bathroom improvements, handwashing facilities and water connections.
For instance, KWFT’s Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) financing solutions support households to construct toilets, repair existing facilities and improve bathrooms and water connections. Through its Kisima Loan, the institution also finances water tanks for rainwater harvesting and storage, water purifiers, shallow wells, water pans and related equipment. Such financing can help families make gradual improvements to their living conditions while spreading the associated costs.
There is also scope to strengthen the role of women entrepreneurs in delivering essential water-related services. Women operating water-selling businesses, for example, can benefit from working capital to maintain stock and financing for equipment that improves efficiency and expands their services. Supporting these enterprises contributes to local service delivery while creating income-generating opportunities.
The benefits of improved sanitation are particularly significant for women and girls. Access to adequate household facilities can ease the responsibilities associated with water collection and sanitation management, while safe and private toilets in schools support menstrual hygiene, protect girls’ dignity and help reduce absenteeism. Improving sanitation therefore contributes not only to better health but also to women’s economic participation and girls’ educational opportunities.
These outcomes reinforce the connection between sanitation and broader development priorities, including Sustainable Development Goal 6 on clean water and sanitation, SDG 3 on good health and well-being, and SDG 5 on gender equality.
As we mark World Toilet Day, there is an opportunity to strengthen collaboration among government, financial institutions, development partners and the private sector to expand access to safe and affordable sanitation. Continued public investment in infrastructure, policy support and targeted interventions for vulnerable households can be complemented by private-sector financing and the provision of quality sanitation products and services.
Ultimately, improving sanitation requires sustained investment at both household and community levels. Making appropriate financing accessible can help more families take practical steps towards safer facilities, better hygiene and healthier living conditions, contributing to Kenya’s broader sanitation and development ambitions.
The author is the Managing Director, Kenya Women Microfinance Bank PLC.

items.title: T20 the focus as batters bowl and 'Sandpapergate' saga rumbles on
items.summary:
England in Australia: T20 cricket the new focus as batters bowl, Adil Rashid eyes recall and 'Sandpapergate' rumbles on
England begin five-match T20 series against beleaguered Australia in Melbourne on Saturday (8.15am UK); Harry Brook's side looking to build-on ODI series win as Adil Rashid eyes re
items.text:
England in Australia: T20 cricket the new focus as batters bowl, Adil Rashid eyes recall and 'Sandpapergate' rumbles on
England begin five-match T20 series against beleaguered Australia in Melbourne on Saturday (8.15am UK); Harry Brook's side looking to build-on ODI series win as Adil Rashid eyes recall after being omitted for 50-over matches; Mitchell Marsh does not appear at pre-series press conference
Friday 20 November 2026 11:13, UK
"You could see it going horribly wrong, couldn't you? You could see things imploding."
That was Michael Atherton's take on Australia before the 'Sandpapergate' scandal spectacularly hit the headlines once again following Usman Khawaja's claims in his autobiography.
Three weeks ago, the biggest problems for the Baggy Greens were Test batting woes, including a bang-out-of-form Marnus Labuschagne, and some odd selection decisions.
They pale now, though.
- Pat Cummins under pressure after Cameron Bancroft article
- Reaction to Cameron Bancroft's incredible comments
- Listen to latest episode of Sky Sports Cricket Podcast
That "implosion" Athers predicted on the field has come off it, with David Warner and Cameron Bancroft supporting Khawaja's account that all members of the team were aware of the sandpaper scheme in 2018, and Pat Cummins strenuously denying it.
Australian cricket is at civil war and there is no obvious end in sight.
Questions abound (will Cummins survive as captain? Will Steve Smith, Nathan Lyon and Josh Hazlewood have their say? Does Cricket Australia have any choice but to launch a fresh investigation and not just an open forum?) but answers are in short supply.
England looking to pile more misery on Australia
Runs were also in short supply for Australia in the final two ODIs against England as a side helmed by Mitchell Marsh in the absence of the rested (but surely mentally tired) Cummins were twice bundled out in the low 200s chasing targets of 320-plus.
That meant Harry Brook's tourists were able to bounce back from being pummelled in Perth in the opening fixture - a result which brought back horrible memories of their Ashes thrashing at the venue a year ago - to claim a come-from-behind 2-1 series win.
They will now look to pile the misery on their beleaguered hosts with victory in a five-match T20 international series, starting in Melbourne on Saturday (first ball at 8.15am UK time).
At times in the ODIs, it felt like England were toying with an Australia team whose minds were perhaps understandably elsewhere. Jofra Archer sent out to bat at No 6 in Hobart, for example, and also Brook and Tom Banton being asked to deliver their part-time off-spin.
If Archer's elevation was a one-off - it certainly won't be seen in the T20s with the England quick rested as he prepares for the three-Test assignment in South Africa from December 17 - then the use of Brook and Banton with the ball may be a more regular occurrence, especially in 50-over cricket as Brendon McCullum's side laser in on the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.
Head coach McCullum said: "These guys are talented, there is something there.
"We are looking at a World Cup in 12 months' time, and no one knows what the conditions are going to be like. You could end up on a pitch that is exploding and need some options.
"We will keep encouraging them to do that. That World Cup is potentially 13 games in three different countries, fresh pitches, there's not much data on how those pitches will play."
Marsh not expected to attend press conferences during series
Brook and Banton bowled 2.5 overs between them in the ODI series, which is 2.5 overs more than Adil Rashid. The frontline spinner had ample time to pour over the sandpaper storm after being left out for all three games, with Liam Dawson once again favoured.
Rashid will hope to be recalled for the T20s, starting at the weekend on a ground where he helped England beat Pakistan in the 2022 T20 World Cup final. The 38-year-old has played in all 19 of his side's T20Is in 2026, appearing alongside Dawson in 18 of them.
Brook, like Rashid, has fond memories of the MCG. He, too, was part of the T20 World Cup-winning squad four years ago, while he top-scored in a blink-and-you'll-miss-it, two-day Ashes Test there last winter as England claimed their only win of a sobering tour.
Brook was all smiles during his pre-series media duties in Melbourne on Friday, saying he wanted to guide his side to a 4-0 lead over Australia before he departs for the South Africa tour ahead of the series finale in Canberra on December 2.
He also spoke of his excitement that the uncapped James Coles, Henry Crocombe, Eddie Jack and Thomas Rew were able to experience being in an England squad in Australia, albeit without confirming if or when they would make their T20I debuts.
We do not know how Australia skipper Marsh is feeling, though, with the 34-year-old not expected to engage in any media activity with the written press throughout the T20 leg following Bancroft's explosive claims in that detail-filled account in the West Australian.
Marsh was part of the XI for the now infamous Cape Town Test eight years ago.
Cummins, Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc will not feature in the series at all as chat regarding what they did or did not know about the sandpaper use runs rampant.

items.text:
Mikel Arteta has said Bukayo Saka may not return before Christmas as the Arsenal forward continues his rehabilitation from a thigh injury.
Saka has been out since limping off against Bayern Munich at the end of last month, and it is understood he has yet to resume light training. Arteta revealed more tests during the international break confirmed the England forward did not need surgery and that he was expected to be out for another four weeks.
When asked whether Saka could be fit for the game against Manchester United on 20 December, Arteta was unsure. “I cannot be that specific,” he said. “In four weeks’ time a lot of things can happen. Maybe it is three and then it is five.
“At the end, there are a few elements. One is the healing of that tissue – and we cannot predict exactly when that tissue is going to be in the best condition to push it. Then there is the rehab plan that we have now, what he needs to do in the gym, what he needs to do in terms of treatment and on the field.”
Arsenal will also be without Martín Zubimendi for Saturday’s trip to Newcastle after the Spain midfielder picked up a hamstring injury against England last Sunday. Otherwise Arteta has a clean bill of health, with William Saliba poised to return after a long-term back injury, although Max Dowman remains suspended after his red card against Fleetwood.
Christos Tzolis is expected to start but Arteta revealed Arsenal’s players were now banned from selecting themselves or any teammates in the Fantasy Premier League game after the Greece forward’s team was leaked before the win over Liverpool on 1 November. Tzolis had been out injured for several weeks but picked himself for the trip to Anfield, alerting their opponents. He is believed to have played his wildcard to remove all the Arsenal players from his squad.
“We haven’t dealt with it [before] and I wanted to put new things in place,” said Arteta. “But obviously confidentiality is something critical because it’s about trust and about what you are trying to do. That should be kept as a huge secret and we’ll take measures to make sure it doesn’t happen.”

items.text:
Introducing Frostbite: A new CPU architecture discovered, designed, and verified end-to-end by AI
Abstract
In our previous post, Redwood, we showed that given an architecture, our AI systems could implement, verify, and deploy an inference accelerator in record time. However, similar to other scientific domains, we believe that AI systems, given the correct freedom and guardrails, can co-design software and hardware together, making optimizations across the stack and opening a design space so large it was previously inaccessible. We set out to answer the question: “Could our AI systems & tools lead to a novel hardware discovery that radically outperforms human-made designs?”
Today, we're introducing Frostbite, a general-purpose CPU with a new instruction set built from the ground up. Frostbite exploits the properties of interaction nets, namely that every step is local, every dependency is explicit, and every value has exactly one owner, to reach a step-function gain in CPU performance that has long stagnated. On a set of 25 initially chosen workloads, including 15 held out until the final evaluation, we achieved a 4.59x performance-per-watt multiple when compared to a modern, silicon-proven superscalar (dual-issue, in-order) CPU core.
Our AI systems autonomously iterated over the compiler, ISA, architecture, microarchitecture, RTL, verification, and final GDS. When we took a closer look at the discovered architectural primitives, we were surprised to find novel hardware implementations and runtime features that would have otherwise been difficult to architect. In spite of stagnation in CPU core improvement, we were able to take a workload concept all the way to a final GDS, and prove a step-function increase in perf/W and perf/area. We believe that as AI systems become more capable, every class of chip we know today, from datacenter-grade CPUs, to AI accelerators, to networking switches and NICs, will go through similar fundamental architectural shifts.
Introduction to interaction nets
Mainstream programming languages, when compiled for general-purpose CPUs, hide the dependencies between the parts of a program. Any piece of code may read or write any variable through a shared, mutable state, and so modern CPU hardware assumes the worst case and rediscovers, at runtime, which instructions actually depend on each other. Moreover, single-core CPU performance has largely stalled since the early 2000s, pushing people towards large multicore CPUs such as Intel Xeon, AMD Zen, and NVIDIA Vera. This forces CPUs to maintain the illusion that every core sees the same memory, and keeping that illusion consistent and performant requires deep cache hierarchies and coherence protocols that cost area and power, and scale poorly.
Interaction nets1 take a different approach. A program is a graph of nodes, and computation happens by rewriting pairs of nodes that are connected through their ports. Every rewrite only touches a small, local part of the graph. Because each node has exactly one principal port, no two of these active pairs ever overlap, so they can be rewritten in any order, or all at once, and the result is always the same. Interaction nets are also linear: every value is used exactly once, so there is no shared mutable state for the hardware to guard. Languages such as Vine2compile ordinary-looking programs directly to interaction nets. For an excellent introduction to interaction nets and why they suit hardware, we highly recommend Tendrils' “On Interaction Nets.” 3
Fig. 1 shows the difference on a small search problem, placing five queens on a five-by-five board. The sequential program visits one candidate at a time. The interaction net exposes all of its independent work: on average, about twelve interactions are ready to run at every step. Nothing about the program was rewritten to get this parallelism; the dependencies were simply never thrown away.
In theory, this should have two large advantages. The first is multithreading for free: rather than varying levels of coarse and fine-grained parallelism, parallelism comes straight from the program. No threads, locks, or race conditions, and none of the out-of-order machinery a conventional core uses to dig it back out. The second is that, since every value has one owner and every step is local, data can live in small local memories next to where it is used. That removes much of the area and power a conventional chip spends on large caching subsystems, and much of the system-level complexity of keeping those caches coherent.
Process
Frostbite was designed with zero architectural priors. We followed the process below, riding multiple agent swarms along the way.
Architecture exploration and selection
To begin architectural exploration, we had to establish the set of workloads Frostbite should do exceedingly well in. We decided to look at different ways a program could expose its work: many independent pieces at once, rounds of parallel work, long sequential chains, data-dependent branches, and recursion. Under each category, we created a search set and a held-out eval set to evaluate the final Frostbite on, ensuring the design generalized to programs it was never tuned on. The kernels for FFT, radixsort, and LU follow the implementation in the SPLASH-2 benchmark, although 64 times smaller, because at regular sizes they are not suitable for exploratory work.
Later, we added five more practical workloads to the held-out set: a Kalman filter, PCA, finite element analysis, an LU solve, and LZ4 decompression.
Agents synthesized research papers and existing benchmarks, and built Python models to trade off high-level architectural ideas against each other, before narrowing to a single architectural concept. The output of this exploration was a 141-page PDF covering the proposed programming model, the runtime, and the high-level blocks of the chip. This was nowhere near the final architecture, but rather a starting point where all the prior findings,

items.text:
Thomas Frank: What should Crystal Palace expect from their new manager, what does he need to change - and can he keep the Eagles up?
Thomas Frank takes charge of Crystal Palace for the first time on Saturday as the Eagles face Coventry at the Coventry Building Society Arena; Frank's new side sit bottom of the Premier League table after two wins from their first 10 matches
Thursday 19 November 2026 12:21, UK
One of the Premier League's most charismatic managers is back.
On November 16, Thomas Frank signed a deal running until the summer of 2029 to take over the vacant managerial role at Crystal Palace, following the conclusion of Pierre Sage's short spell at Selhurst Park.
His return to the top flight comes nine months after he was sacked by Tottenham after a run of just seven wins in 26 Premier League games.
- Thomas Frank appointed Crystal Palace manager
- Transfer Centre LIVE! | Crystal Palace news & transfers🦅
- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺
Before that, he had four successful Premier League seasons with Brentford, after guiding them to promotion in 2020/21.
Here, Sky Sports takes a look at what Frank needs to change, what to expect in terms of style and shape and whether he can keep Palace in the Premier League...
What situation has he walked into?
Palace won the Conference League last season, so it's easy to forget they also only finished six points above the Premier League relegation zone.
Sage was unable to build on the legacy left by Oliver Glasner, so the Eagles again find themselves in a spot of bother.
The Premier League's bottom side have lost four in succession and have the worst defensive record in the division, having conceded an average of 2.4 goals per game.
They are through to the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup, however, and have taken five points from four Europa League league phase matches so far, which has them currently on course to qualify for the knockout rounds.
Frank highlights issues to address
Speaking in his first interview with the club, Frank identified the problems his new side need to address.
"There's no doubt - to state the obvious - we need to stabilise things. We need to work incredibly hard," he said.
"We are conceding too many goals, so we need to work on the defensive side of things, with principles, attitude. We need to work on set-pieces, which are key in both boxes. We need to work on defensive transitions, as we are conceding too many situations there.
"We need to bring energy, belief, confidence because this is a very, very good team and very good players, but they need to believe in themselves.
"We need to balance a lot of things with aiming high in Europe and two fantastic cup tournaments, but the Premier League is the most important, if we need to prioritise."
What needs to change then?
Analysis by Sky Sports News' Chris Reidy:
Frank will see areas all over the pitch he can improve for Crystal Palace, but undoubtedly his priority will be to stop them conceding as many goals and as many chances as they have so far this season.
Crystal Palace have kept one clean sheet in the Premier League this season and too often look vulnerable on transitions and weak on set-pieces.
Frank will have to review whether the personnel he has suits playing three centre-halves or if a change to four is necessary. Time and time again teams have exploited space between defenders against Crystal Palace which leads to shots or good chances created for the opposition.
Away from the defence, Frank will need to rejuvenate Adam Wharton. The midfielder has been way off his best this season, and perhaps finding the right partner for him will be key to that. Quinten Timber has shown plenty of energy and will in his early days at Palace perhaps without giving stability in the middle, and Daichi Kamada has been used higher up the pitch due to Ismaila Sarr's absence from the team.
What has gone under the radar in recent weeks because of Crystal Palace's defending, is their struggles up top. Eddie Nketiah's fortunate penalty with the last kick of the game against Liverpool spared Palace a record of four Premier League games without a goal.
Crystal Palace have spent the most time trailing in the league and have also only taken the lead in three games this season. A mentality shift is needed, because Palace have good players who aren't responding well to adversity.
What should fans expect in terms of style?
Based on his previous jobs, Frank has shown he is a pragmatic manager, not wedded to one shape or style and comfortable finding different ways to win.
His most used formation in the Premier League is a 4-3-3 (59), but he has also heavily used a 4-2-3-1 (35) or - importantly for Crystal Palace - a 3-5-2 (53).
Across his four top-flight seasons at Brentford, the Bees scored 80 set-piece goals, with only Arsenal, Liverpool and Man City scoring more across that period.
He is reportedly close to adding Bernardo Cueva - his former set-piece coach at Brentford - to his coaching staff, which suggests a similar approach is likely at Selhurst Park.
Elsewhere, while the Bees became markedly more direct after promotion from the Championship, there was still a particular focus on high quality chances, meaning fewer shots were taken from outside the box.
From 1763 shots across their first four seasons in the Premier League, Frank's Brentford created 225.0 worth of Expected Goals, which equated to a league-high 0.128 xG per shot.
So why didn't it work out at Spurs?
Analysis by Sky Sports News' Michael Bridge:
"It just didn't seem the right fit from the start. It didn't get off to the best of starts in terms of the press conference when he said: 'We will 100 per cent lose football matches.' Then he turned to the press office and said: 'Apart from Arsenal.' The problem is, when you say something at a club like Spurs, it stays.
"There were some really tough defeats for Spurs fans to look at.

I only got eight this week, can you do any better? It’s sports quiz of the week:
United drone update: operator issues apology
A drone operator who filmed Manchester United’s training session this week has apologised for what he called a “total error of judgment” and removed the footage from his YouTube channel.
The footage, filmed at United’s Carrington training ground during new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session on Thursday, was uploaded online under the username CC Overview. In a statement posted on his YouTube channel on Friday, the drone operator said that while the flight was legal under drone regulations, filming the session had been “unethical”.
“My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time,” he said. “I fully accept it was unethical on my part. I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.”
The operator added that he had wrongly assumed only warm-up activities would be visible and that the training session would be open to various media outlets. He also said neither Liverpool nor any other football club had been involved in his decision to film at Carrington. “The video has been removed from my channel,” he said.
Bruno Guimarães to feel the heat on Tyneside, Alex Scott’s return further cheers Cherries and Manchester City face favourite whipping boys… here are your 10 things to look out for in the Premier League this weekend:
Fifa news … Kozo Tashima said he hasn’t talked yet with fellow Fifa presidential race challenfer Philippe Diallo, but he’s willing to work with the Frenchman to defeat Gianni Infantino’s bid for a controversial fourth term.
Tashima and Diallo are two long-shot candidates to replace Infantino in an election set for 18 March. So there’s still plenty time to sway Fifa’s 211 member federations.
“We do share some moral or ethical positions, so he’s a great person to team up with,” Tashima said in comments translated from Japanese. “I’m not looking at Diallo as opposition. I just want to change Fifa. Diallo is also very strict in governance and he does have a lot of experience in management. I do trust him. At this point I’m not think about withdrawing.”
Tashima, who repeated the words “integrity, fairness, trust and transparency” when asked why he decided to stand, is going against the endorsement of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), which last month pledged support for Infantino — with Infantino on hand at the meeting in Tokyo.
“I just don’t only want to be the Fifa president, my intention was to make Fifa better,” Tashima added. “Being the president is the shortcut to making that happen. I just want to clean up the federation and make it a fair organization. I want to help rebuild the whole organisation.
“I believe the worst outcome would be for him (Infantino) to remain in office without an election,” he said. “I believe this is a test of whether Fifa truly has the capacity for self-reform. “He’s done a lot of things to make us doubt his integrity,” Tashima said, adding that income from the World Cup – or anywhere else – “is not an Infantino asset. It belongs to Fifa.”
In a three-candidate election, votes from two-thirds of the eligible members are needed to win in the first round. For the second round, the candidate with the fewest votes is eliminated and a simple majority will win. In a two-candidate race, Infantino would need votes from 106 of the 211 member federations to win re-election.
Drone footage of Pochettino’s first training session posted on YouTube
Footage from Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session as Manchester United manager has appeared online after being captured by a drone operator. A 12-minute video of the session was posted on to YouTube by an account called CC OVERVIEW after being captured at United’s Carrington training ground. Pochettino and his United players can be seen in the video, with the squad having been divided into three groups.
On the post, the drone operator wrote: “For the people asking about legality. It is unrestricted airspace, meaning anyone can fly over it. The drone remained in line of sight at all times, it didn’t fly over anyone or even near anyone so was a perfectly legal flight going by the CAA rules that regulates drone usage.
“The drone is correctly labelled, and I hold all the relevant licences, public liability and insurance required. As for leaking team news/tactics, it was half an hour into the manager’s first training session, there are many media there so certainly won’t be the only footage of training released.”
Manchester United have declined to comment.
Pochettino was taking his first training session after being appointed as United’s new head coach last week, succeeding Michael Carrick who was sacked with the club in the relegation zone during this international window. Pochettino arrived in Manchester on Wednesday, having taken charge of the United States for the final time in their 2-0 win over Haiti, which finished in the early hours of Wednesday morning UK time. His first match in charge will be a visit to old rivals Liverpool on Sunday afternoon. Press Association

items.text:
If you can’t explain something in simple terms, you don’t understand it
In the early 1960s, Richard Feynman gave a series of undergraduate lectures that were collected into a book called the Feynman Lectures on Physics. Absent from the book was a lecture Feynman gave on planetary motion, but a later finding of the notes enabled David Goodstein, a colleague of Feynman’s, to write a book about it: Feynman’s Lost Lecture. From an excerpt of the book published in a 1996 issue of Caltech’s Engineering & Science magazine:
Feynman was a truly great teacher. He prided himself on being able to devise ways to explain even the most profound ideas to beginning students. Once, I said to him, “Dick, explain to me, so that I can understand it, why spin one-half particles obey Fermi-Dirac statistics.” Sizing up his audience perfectly, Feynman said, “I’ll prepare a freshman lecture on it.” But he came back a few days later to say, “I couldn’t do it. I couldn’t reduce it to the freshman level. That means we don’t really understand it.”
John Gruber writes the simple explanations are the goal at Apple as well:
Engineers are expected to be able to explain a complex technology or product in simple, easily-understood terms not because the executive needs it explained simply to understand it, but as proof that the engineer understands it completely.
Feynman was well known for simple explanations of scientific concepts that result a in deeper understanding of the subject matter: e.g. see Feynman explaining how fire is stored sunshine, rubber bands, how trains go around curves, and magnets. Critically, he’s also not shy about admitting when he doesn’t understand something…or, alternately, when scientists as a group don’t understand something. There’s the spin anecdote above and of his explanation of magnets, he says:
I really can’t do a good job, any job, of explaining magnetic force in terms of something else you’re more familiar with, because I don’t understand it in terms of anything else you’re more familiar with.
Feynman was also quoted as saying:
I think I can safely say that nobody understands quantum mechanics.
Pretty interesting thing to hear from a guy who won a Nobel Prize for explaining quantum mechanics better than anyone ever had before. Even when he died in 1988 at the end of a long and fruitful careeer, a note at the top of his blackboard read:
What I cannot create, I do not understand.

items.title: Signal Is Serious About Protecting Your Privacy
items.summary:

items.text:
Privacy is our mission; it’s why we exist, and we do everything we can to protect it.
This means that we are restricting the latest AI agents built into mobile operating systems from potentially capturing and storing your Signal data.
We’ve already had to do this once with Windows. Last year, we used screenshot blocking to prevent Microsoft’s Recall AI from taking and storing screenshots of your Signal messages on Windows 11 operating systems by default.1 We will now be taking similar measures to restrict agentic systems built into iOS 27 and on Android versions where we can detect an AI assistant attempting to read your Signal screen.2
The problem is similar to Microsoft Recall on Windows: Google and Apple are integrating agentic capabilities like Gemini Intelligence with Google Gemini and Onscreen Awareness with Siri AI deep into their operating systems. This is a significant move. Google (Android), Apple (iOS/macOS), and Microsoft (Windows) produce the three major consumer operating systems (OS), which comprise the environment that third-party developers – like Signal – build their apps to function and operate within. To put it differently, these three operating systems are the oceans in which Signal, and other applications, must swim; they dictate the conditions of life for the application ecosystem. Right now, these agentic AI integrations are changing this environment in a way that’s making it increasingly hostile to privacy. This is an existential threat to Signal, and our ability to responsibly uphold our mission.
In order to gain access to information about you, these OS AI agents “scan” the information that’s on your screen. In doing so, your Signal data is captured, then made available to these agentic systems in order to allow them to answer your questions and do your bidding.
The net result is that these AI capabilities in the operating system are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy. For over a decade, this guarantee has been backed by our tried and trusted open source code base and our formally verified encryption protocol. These have been scrutinized by some of the best security experts and hackers across the world, and shown to be robust. Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment. All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.
So, we are blocking such capture by preventing screenshots in the app on iOS 27 and when AI assistants attempt to capture screen data on Android.2
People who want the ability to take screenshots can disable this protection within the Signal app’s settings. However, doing so will potentially expose your (and your contacts’) Signal content to these AI agents, and break our privacy guarantees. Our remedy is also incomplete – while we are doing everything we can, restricting screenshots does not address other more sneaky ways AI agents could potentially access application data, such as retrieving content already present on a user’s device via the filesystem.
We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy. Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience. This is also the reason we are currently unable to implement these protections on macOS.3
We are also struggling with a significant lack of documentation about how these AI agents actually work. Over the past few months, we’ve spent considerable developer time and energy doing forensic investigations across Android and iOS in an attempt to learn what is actually happening when these AI systems access application data. Without better documentation and clear technical specifications, it will be increasingly difficult for Signal to provide robust privacy and security to the many millions of people who rely on us.
We continue to call on the major consumer operating system companies – Apple, Google, and Microsoft – to provide simple technical tools and accurate documentation that give developers like Signal ways to prevent AI agents from accessing sensitive application data. In particular, we are calling on these companies to provide two common-sense remedies that can protect the privacy so many millions of people rely on:
- Developers should have an easy and well-documented way to opt their app out of AI data access and processing, including (but not limited to) screen reading, filesystem access, notifications, APIs, and other OS frameworks, all without undermining the core utility of an application.
- Operating system companies should create better documentation and technical specifications around how these AI agents function, particularly regarding data access and processing. Confidential computing approaches are not a complete solution, and do not address these core concerns. In particular, these approaches still leave the power to determine the extent of privacy guarantees (if any) in the hands of these providers.
We also see a growing need for tools that can prevent third-party agents, like Meta’s Muse, from accessing application data using the deep permissions that users are encouraged to grant them during setup. In many cases these agents are leveraging accessibility settings that were meant to empower actual people to get the most out of their apps and services, not to act as a skeleton key that provides access to AI agents.
In addition to taking these technical measures to block capture, we are engaging in conversations across the ecosystem to make the stakes clear. There is a lot of work to be done in the i

items.title: Guimaraes growing at Arsenal - but Arteta still wants more
items.summary:
Bruno Guimaraes: Arsenal midfielder is growing in stature but Mikel Arteta still wants more from Brazilian ahead of Newcastle return
Bruno Guimaraes is set to return to Newcastle in Arsenal colours, but even though he has worked his way into the Gunners team Mikel Arteta is still not completely happ
items.text:
Bruno Guimaraes: Arsenal midfielder is growing in stature but Mikel Arteta still wants more from Brazilian ahead of Newcastle return
Bruno Guimaraes is set to return to Newcastle in Arsenal colours, but even though he has worked his way into the Gunners team Mikel Arteta is still not completely happy; watch Newcastle vs Arsenal live on Sky Sports this Saturday from 5pm, kick-off 5.30pm
Friday 20 November 2026 09:50, UK
It's all eyes on Bruno Guimaraes this Saturday. The Newcastle hero who captained the team to cup success returns in Arsenal colours. And he returns as a growing cog in the Gunners' system.
Despite being Newcastle's key man, the Brazilian endured a slow start to life at Arsenal. An early-season injury did not help, nor did the early-season form of Myles Lewis-Skelly in the Brazilian's absence.
But now he is back in the North East as a first-choice option, having impressed in Arsenal's recent league wins over Liverpool and Hull, while also scoring crucial goals against Sunderland and Leeds.
But is Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta satisfied? Not yet.
"He's still not there," said Arteta after the 1-0 win over Hull last time out. "He's much better, he's hitting serious levels now, but we can still take the player to another level."
The comments were a surprise, given Guimaraes had just received a standing ovation from the Arsenal crowd as he was substituted following an impressive display.
- Transfer Centre LIVE! | Arsenal news & transfers🔴⚪
- Arsenal fixtures & scores | FREE Arsenal highlights▶️
- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺
In a largely frustrating game for the Gunners before Martin Odegaard's second-half winner, the Brazilian was at the heart of the action. He recorded more touches and passes than any other Arsenal player, while he was equally effective in the defensive side of the game.
When Arteta made attacking substitutions in search of a winner, he took Declan Rice off before Guimaraes. That is how well he was playing - but it is still not enough for the Arsenal manager.
"I told him in the dressing room - he's very good, he had a massive impact, he owned a lot of moments in the game," said Arteta. "But there is still much more to come."
Pushed on those comments this week, he said: "It's about impact, the amount of things he can do to influence the game and own the game."
To work out what Arteta is getting at, it is worth going back to the analysis the Spaniard made of his £75m signing when he first joined.
"A player which obviously has tremendous timing and intuition to win the ball back and progress play very, very fast," said Arteta back in August.
"He's a player that is very comfortable putting people through, moving between the lines, moving in behind."
Winning the ball back and playing it forward very fast are two areas where Guimaraes has excelled so far this season.
From a defensive point of view, only Chelsea's Romeo Lavia has a better ground-duel success rate this season among Premier League midfielders.
His ball-winning ability was no better seen than his roar of delight in front of the Arsenal fans in the first half of the win at Anfield, after he stopped a dangerous Liverpool attack into the penalty area.
But, as Arteta says, Guimaraes also gets the ball forward - and quickly. The numbers back that up too. He ranks very highly among Premier League midfielders for line-breaking passes.
But perhaps this is where Arteta is demanding more from the Brazilian. Rice is one of the top two or three players at line-breaking passes and Guimaraes - who plays with the England midfielder in a double pivot - has slightly lower numbers.
If Rice is the standard in Arteta's eyes, then Guimaraes has work to do to reach that level.
Another area where Guimaraes could improve is scoring goals. He netted nine Premier League goals last season and it was another key skill that Arteta identified back in August.
"He's got a smell and a really good timing to get in the box," he said. "And he has the capacity to finish the actions."
Now, Guimaraes has already shown his goalscoring prowess against Sunderland and Leeds, but they were strikes from the edge of the area. Useful, yes - but they are not classic Guimaraes goals.
Just seven of the Brazilian's Premier League goals for Newcastle came from outside the penalty area, with the remaining 24 coming from inside the penalty box. Guimaraes is yet to show the close-range threat that Arteta rates so much.
He seemingly has a lot to do to reach the levels Rice is hitting - but that is not an easy feat.
In a recent interview with GQ Magazine, Rice revealed how it can take up to a year to get used to Arteta's demands in midfield.
Rice remembered seeing Christian Norgaard - another midfielder who arrived at Arsenal with plenty of Premier League experience - struggle to keep up. "You're not going to grasp this for like six, seven months," Rice recalled about what he said to Norgaard.
Arteta recognises that too. "He's getting better at it," he said this week. "And he will get better at it when the relationships and understanding of what we do increases day by day."
"With our manager, he doesn't care who you are," Rice added. "You're getting detail. You're going into the game knowing everything."
Guimaraes is feeling that harsh side of Arteta right now. Even though he is playing and performing, there is plenty of work still to do.

items.title: Carnival Cruises emits ten times more sulphur oxide than all of Europe's cars (2019)
items.summary: In April, Ecohustler disrupted Carnival Cruise's AGM calling on the shareholders to reduce their company's pollution using straight forward and affordable methods - like burning cleaner fuel. Since then, a new report outlines the corporation's impact on the coastline of Europe. These vast floating c
items.text:
In April, Ecohustler disrupted Carnival Cruise's AGM calling on the shareholders to reduce their company's pollution using straight forward and affordable methods - like burning cleaner fuel. Since then, a new report outlines the corporation's impact on the coastline of Europe. These vast floating cities are burning dirty bunker fuel and creating shocking levels of air pollution wherever they go. Shipping has been an unregulated industry for too long and action is urgently required.
Carnival Corporation, the world’s largest luxury cruise operator, emitted nearly 10 times more sulphur oxide (SOx) around European coasts than did all 260 million European cars in 2017, a new analysis by sustainable transport group Transport & Environment reveals.
Royal Caribbean Cruises, the world’s second largest, is second, yet four times worse than the European car fleet. SOx emissions form sulphate (SO4) aerosols that increase human health risks and contribute to acidification in terrestrial and aquatic environments.
SUPPORTED BY HEROES LIKE YOU
Support independent eco journalism that drives real change.
In absolute terms, Spain, Italy and Greece, closely followed by France and Norway, are the European countries most exposed to SOx air pollution from cruise vessels while Barcelona, Palma de Mallorca and Venice are the most impacted European port cities, followed by Civitavecchia (Rome) and Southampton.
All photos by Greg English ©
These countries are so exposed because they are major tourist destinations, but also because they have less stringent marine sulphur fuel standards which allows cruise ships to burn the dirtiest most sulphurous fuel all along their coastlines.
Faig Abbasov, shipping policy manager at T&E, said: “Luxury cruise ships are floating cities powered by some of the dirtiest fuel possible. Cities are rightly banning dirty diesel cars but they’re giving a free pass to cruise companies that spew out toxic fumes that do immeasurable harm both to those on board and on nearby shores. This is unacceptable.“
NOX emissions from cruise ships in Europe also heavily impact some cities, equivalent to about 15% of the nitrogen oxides (NOx) emitted by Europe’s passenger car fleet in a year, the report finds. In Marseille, for example, 57 cruise ships emitted in 2017 almost as much NOx as one-quarter of the city’s 340,000 passenger cars. Along the coasts of countries such as Norway, Denmark, Greece, Croatia and Malta a handful of cruise ships are also responsible for more NOx than the majority of their domestic car fleet.
Europe should implement a zero-emission port standard as soon as possible, this could then be extended to other ship types. The report also recommends extending emission control areas (ECAs), currently in place only in the North and Baltic Seas and English Channel, to the rest of the European seas. Furthermore, the report recommends regulating NOx emissions from existing ships, which are currently exempt from NOx standards applying in emission control areas.
Faig Abbasov concluded “There are enough mature technologies to clean up cruise ships. Shore-side electricity can help cut in-port emissions, batteries are a solution for shorter distances and hydrogen technology can power even the biggest cruise ships. The cruise sector are apparently not willing to make the shift voluntarily, so we need governments to step in and mandate zero emission standards.”

items.text:
Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide
- Published
Nigerian President Bola Tinubu has asked parliament to decriminalise attempted suicide, proposing medical support instead of prosecution for those who survive.
The proposal seeks to shift Nigeria's approach from criminal punishment to treatment and rehabilitation.
It follows years of calls for reform from mental health professionals. A separate bill seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide has already passed its second reading in the Senate.
Under Nigeria's law, attempted suicide is a criminal offence with those convicted facing up to one year's imprisonment, a fine or both.
The Senate bill also seeks to replace criminal penalties for attempted suicide with medical treatment, rehabilitation and support.
It was sponsored by Senator Asuquo Ekpenyong, who has argued that prosecuting people who survive suicide attempts could discourage those experiencing suicidal thoughts from seeking help.
He also warned that families might conceal such incidents for fear of prosecution and social stigma.
He stressed that the bill is not aimed at legalising or encouraging suicide attempts but rather protecting the survivors.
Tinubu's proposal has been welcomed by Senate President Godswill Akpabio, who had previously suggested that people who survived suicide attempts should be sent to prison.
"We are saying that suicide is a crime for now. Therefore, if you attempt it, we will send you to prison," Akpabio had said.
However, after receiving the Tinubu's proposal, he sought to clarify his earlier remarks, saying they did not apply to people experiencing mental health conditions.
He added that punishing people whose actions were influenced by mental health conditions would be insensitive.
Tinubu's letter follows sustained calls from mental health professionals for the law to be changed.
At a parliamentary public hearing in May 2024, the then president of the Association of Psychiatrists of Nigeria, Professor Taiwo Obindo, urged lawmakers to remove criminal penalties for attempted suicide.
"Why do we, as a nation, then punish individuals who are ill and need medical attention rather than prosecution?" he asked.
Drawing on his experience as a psychiatrist, Obindo said most people who die by suicide have a history of mental illness.
Akpabio has referred the president's amendment bill to the relevant senate committee for further consideration.
Nigeria is among several African countries where attempted suicide remains a criminal offence.
Ghana decriminalised attempted suicide in 2023, while Kenya's High Court ruled in January 2025 that the law criminalising it was unconstitutional.

items.text:
If you find FFmpeg useful, you are welcome to contribute by donating. More downloading options
Get packages & executable files
FFmpeg only provides source code. Below are some links that provide it already compiled and ready to go.
Linux Packages
Linux Static Builds
Windows EXE Files
Get the Sources
You can retrieve the source code through Git by using the command:
git clone https://git.ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg.git ffmpeg
FFmpeg has always been a very experimental and developer-driven project. It is a key component in many multimedia projects and has new features added constantly. Development branch snapshots work really well 99% of the time so people are not afraid to use them.
Git Repositories
Since FFmpeg is developed with Git, multiple repositories from developers and groups of developers are available.
Release Verification
All FFmpeg releases are cryptographically signed with our public PGP key and should be verified for authenticity.
pub   rsa2048 2011-04-26 [SC]
    FCF986EA15E6E293A5644F10B4322F04D67658D8
uid           [  full  ] FFmpeg release signing key <ffmpeg-devel@ffmpeg.org>
sub   rsa2048 2011-04-26 [E]
  To verify a release:
- Import our public key into your local keyring:
        $ curl https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-devel.asc | gpg --import
- Download a release tarball and its corresponding signature.
- 
        Verify the signature:
        $ gpg --verify ffmpeg-4.3.2.tar.xz.asc ffmpeg-4.3.2.tar.xz gpg: Signature made Sun 21 Feb 2021 06:35:15 AEST gpg: using RSA key FCF986EA15E6E293A5644F10B4322F04D67658D8 gpg: issuer "ffmpeg-devel@ffmpeg.org" gpg: Good signature from "FFmpeg release signing key <ffmpeg-devel@ffmpeg.org>" [full]
Optionally, you can verify that git and tarball match, the only differences should be the absence of .git* files in the tarball and a VERSION file in the tarball containing the version. The git tags should be signed with EDDSA key DD1EC9E8DE085C629B3E1846B18E8928B3948D64
    A release that also has a .pq.asc file carries post-quantum
    signatures (RFC 9980)
    made with both of these keys:
  
ML-DSA-87+Ed448  99669C49693683D51F174FE0D9E84915F5C2A536F5C0DA70FB8DCBD8AA8C4B3D
SLH-DSA-256s     547721479F80449E77748C0235116A1F8A73D9ECA98673B90E4E39347D229989
GnuPG cannot verify these yet; use sq 1.4 or later built with a cryptographic backend that supports these algorithms (OpenSSL 3.5 or RustCrypto), both of these must succeed:
$ sq verify --signature-file ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz.pq.asc --signer-file ffmpeg-mldsa87-ed448.cert.pgp ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz
$ sq verify --signature-file ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz.pq.asc --signer-file ffmpeg-slhdsa256s.cert.pgp ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz
Releases
Approximately every 6 months the FFmpeg project makes a new major release. Between major releases point releases will appear that add important bug fixes but no new features. Note that these releases are intended for distributors and system integrators. Users that wish to compile from source themselves are strongly encouraged to consider using the development branch (see above), this is the only version on which FFmpeg developers actively work. The release branches only cherry pick selected changes from the development branch, which therefore receives much more and much faster bug fixes such as additional features and security patches.
